P2700.d: Automatic transmissions shift by filling and releasing clutches or brakes, the friction elements, and the controller learns how long each one takes to apply. P2700 is set when element A engages too slowly, too quickly or not plausibly compared with the commanded shift.
s: Harsh, delayed or slipping shifts involving clutch A
Check engine or transmission warning light on
Incorrect gear ratio codes stored at the same time
c: Worn or damaged clutch A components, such as a cylinder, piston seal or one-way clutch
Sticking valve or solenoid in the main control valve body
Low, aged or incorrect transmission fluid
Adaptive shift values not relearned after repair or software update

P2701.d: P2701 concerns friction element B: the controller has measured an apply time for this clutch or brake that falls outside its learned window. The letter is assigned per gearbox, and bulletins show how varied the causes are.
s: Harsh shifts or engine flare during shifts
One or more gears missing, e.g. no upshift beyond second
Warning light on
c: Mechanical damage in clutch B, such as a displaced snap ring or damaged hub
Damaged one-way clutch working together with element B
Sticking valve or pressure control solenoid for clutch B

P2702.d: With P2702 the transmission controller reports that friction element C does not engage within the time it expects, measured from the shift command to the moment the speed ratio changes. Which clutch C stands for differs between gearbox designs.
s: Harsh or delayed shifts on gears using clutch C
Vehicle may not shift out of Park on some Ford 8F35 units
Wrench or engine warning light on
c: Sticking valves in the main control valve body
Worn clutch C plates or leaking piston seals
Outdated transmission software or lost adaptive values

P2703.d: P2703 points at friction element D: the time it needs to take up torque, as seen from turbine and output speed, no longer matches what the controller has learned. In Ford's eight-speed front-drive units the code turns up with reverse problems.
s: No reverse or harsh engagement into reverse
Harsh or delayed shifts on gears using clutch D
Check engine light on
c: Faulty or contaminated selectable one-way clutch (Ford 8F24/8F35)
Sticking valve in the main control valve body
Worn clutch D plates or leaking seals

P2704.d: P2704 is stored when friction element E takes too long or too short a time to apply, judged against the speed change the controller expects for the shift. Ford bulletins tie the code directly to the E clutch.
s: Harsh engagement into drive or poor shift quality
Wrench, engine or gearbox warning on
Limp mode in a fixed gear on some gearboxes
c: Pressure loss in the E clutch circuit from worn hub or damaged O-rings
Sticking valves in the main control valve body
Transmission control software needing an update
Low fluid level from a leak

P2705.d: P2705 covers the sixth friction element, F, so only transmissions with at least six shift elements use it, such as Ford's ten-speed and eight-speed families. The controller has found that F applies outside the time it has learned.
s: Harsh or slipping shifts in the gears using clutch F
Vehicle may fall back into Park when drive or reverse is selected (Ford 8F57)
Warning light on
c: Sticking valves in the main control valve body
Shift solenoid F not controlling pressure correctly

P2706.d: P2706 is the general code for the sixth shift solenoid, F. Ford's 2024 OBD summary uses it as the base for all shift solenoid F faults in its 10R60/10R80, 8F35/8F40, 8F57 and 8F24 transmissions: with a fault-type byte added, P2706 marks an open, a short to ground, a short to supply, an intermittent connection, stuck off and stuck on, each also carrying its own two-byte code such as P097F, P2707 or P2708.
s: Harsh shifts, missing gears or limp mode
Vehicle may not shift out of Park on some Ford 8F35 units
Warning light on
c: Open or shorted wiring or connector to shift solenoid F, often inside the transmission
Failed shift solenoid F or main control valve body
Control module software that needs reprogramming (Ram 68RFE)
Faulty solenoid driver in the PCM or TCM

P2707.d: P2707 is not an electrical fault: the circuit to shift solenoid F is intact, but the clutch it controls does not apply when commanded, as if the solenoid stayed off. Ford stresses that a ratio-based check cannot tell a solenoid failure apart from other faults in the clutch hydraulics.
s: Gears using clutch F missing or slipping
Return to Park or no engagement in drive or reverse
Check engine light on
c: Leaking or damaged clutch F piston or seals
Shift solenoid F or its valve sticking in the off position
Insufficient supply pressure, e.g. damaged fluid pump gasket

P2708.d: P2708 means the clutch fed by shift solenoid F stays applied when the controller expects it released, although the wiring checks pass. Ford's 2024 OBD summary maps it to P2706 with the failed-on byte 7E for its 10R60/10R80, 8F35/8F40, 8F57 and 8F24 units.
s: Harsh or delayed engagement and shifts
MIL lit, often with other stuck-on or gear-ratio codes
Binding or shudder as two clutches work against each other
Transmission may hold a fixed gear for protection
c: Internal oil leak at a clutch cylinder or sleeve keeping the clutch applied (Ford 10R80 CDF cylinder)
Shift solenoid F mechanically sticking in the applied position (dirt, wear)
Outdated PCM/TCM calibration; Ford bulletins combine reprogramming with the repair
Debris or degraded fluid jamming valves in the valve body

P2709.d: P2709 flags an electrical fault on shift solenoid F, found by the output driver rather than by watching the gearbox shift. Hyundai and Kia list it as the circuit code for that valve: Kia bulletin TRA 051 and Hyundai 15-AT-010 call solenoid F SS-B on their six-speed transaxles and replace parts instead of the gearbox, Kia first the solenoid, then the harness to the PCM, and only then the PCM if the code returns; Hyund
s: MIL lit and transmission in a fail-safe gear
Missing gears or sudden harsh shifts
Code returns immediately after clearing if the fault is permanent
c: Defective coil in shift solenoid F (Hyundai/Kia replace the solenoid first)
Chafed or corroded wiring or connector between PCM/TCM and transmission
Damaged internal transmission harness or lead frame
Faulty output driver in the PCM/TCM

P270A.d: P270A opens a row of six codes (A to F) for an overheated clutch or brake inside the gearbox. The controller keeps track of how hot element A gets when it slips during launches and shifts and sets the code once that value passes its limit; the code is a warning of thermal overload rather than proof of a broken part.
s: Reduced engine power or gearbox warning message
Harsh or slipping engagement of the affected gear
Burnt smell of transmission fluid after heavy use
c: Repeated launches, creeping or towing that load element A with long slip phases
Worn element A slipping because of low apply pressure or worn linings
Low or aged transmission fluid reducing cooling of the clutch
Restricted fluid cooler or faulty cooling valve

P270B.d: P270B concerns the shift element lettered B. A multi-plate clutch has no sensor of its own, so the controller usually derives its heat from the energy turned into warmth while the plates slip and from the oil temperature, then compares the result with a limit.
s: Torque reduction or limited acceleration
Changed shift points or skipped gears
Shudder when element B engages
c: Slow or weak apply of element B creating extra slip (pressure or seal problem)
Stop-and-go, steep grades or trailer loads
Implausible fluid temperature input distorting the calculated value

P270C.d: With P270C the controller reports that clutch or brake C has run hotter than its permitted limit. Typical triggers are long slip phases: creeping in heavy traffic, holding the car on a slope with the throttle, or a trailer launch.
s: Warning in the cluster with reduced power
Gear using element C avoided or held only briefly
Hot, darkened fluid
c: Creeping or holding on a grade with the throttle instead of the brake
Element C slipping from low apply pressure or worn plates
Faulty clutch cooling oil valve or restricted cooler (where fitted)

P270D.d: P270D is stored when the thermal state of shift element D rises above the controller's limit. The heat comes from friction during slip, so anything that lengthens slip on D counts: a sluggish apply, leaking seals in its hydraulic circuit, or hard use with a heavy load.
s: Limited torque or gear range for protection
Transmission temperature warning
Flare or slip on shifts involving element D
c: Leaking seals in the apply circuit of element D lengthening slip
Blocked or undersized fluid cooler, especially when towing
Old or wrong fluid with reduced friction and cooling properties

P270E.d: P270E reports an over-temperature of the shift element labelled E. Because the value is normally calculated rather than measured inside the clutch, a wrong input can also trigger it: an implausible fluid temperature signal or incorrect slip data from the speed sensors would distort the estimate.
s: Gearbox warning with reduced performance
Additional sensor codes stored
Slipping or delayed shifts through element E
c: Faulty fluid temperature or speed sensor signal distorting the calculated temperature
Real slip of element E under load
Poor internal contact in the transmission control electronics

P270F.d: P270F closes the A-to-F series and signals that element F has exceeded its temperature limit. Only gearboxes with at least six shift elements carry a letter F, so the code belongs to modern multi-speed automatics, but no maker publishes its use or thresholds.
s: Torque reduction and warning message
Gears using element F temporarily unavailable
Harsh or slipping shifts
c: Element F slipping due to low pressure or wear
Severe duty such as towing, mountain driving or repeated launches

P2710.d: P2710 is the sporadic counterpart to P2709: the circuit of shift solenoid F drops out now and then and recovers, so a check at standstill often finds nothing. In Ford's 2024 OBD summary it equals P2706 with the intermittent byte 1F in the general solenoid list and in the 8F57 and 8F24 tables; the tables for 10R60/10R80 and 8F35/8F40 instead list P2710 for a short to supply voltage.
s: Occasional harsh shift or brief fail-safe operation
MIL that comes and goes with the fault
No fault found during a static circuit test
c: Loose or spread terminal at the transmission or module connector
Wire rubbing through intermittently inside or outside the case
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Heat-dependent internal break in the solenoid coil

P2711.d: P2711 is set when the transmission controller sees the drivetrain act as if a gear were no longer properly engaged although it never commanded that, for example because a clutch drags or a gear does not engage as selected. Volkswagen Group uses it on DSG gearboxes: Audi bulletin 2029069 for the 2009-2010 A3 and TT logs it as 19143 P2711 004, with a lit gear display and shudder on the first launch, and blames a clutch
s: Gear indicator flashing or lit in the cluster
Shudder on the first drive-away
Selected Drive or Reverse does not engage after start-up
c: Excessive drag torque in the dual clutch (worn or early-production plates)
Shift fork or gear actuator not holding the gear

P2712.d: P2712 targets gearboxes whose clutches or shift forks are worked by a separate hydraulic power unit, typically an electric pump that charges a pressure accumulator. Such a system loses pressure only slowly when sealed; if pressure drops faster than expected or the pump has to recharge too often, the controller concludes there is a leak.
s: Hydraulic pump running often or for long periods
Gears not engaging or delayed engagement
Gearbox warning and emergency mode
c: Internal leakage at valves or seals of the hydraulic unit
External oil leak at housing, lines or connector seals

P2713.d: P2713 is the umbrella code for pressure control solenoid D; it names the valve but not the kind of fault, so the failure type byte behind it carries the detail. Toyota works this way.
s: MIL lit with further transmission codes
Harsh, late or missing shifts
Whine noise or reduced power in some vehicles
c: Internal transmission damage that makes the valve or its clutch stick (Toyota replaces the unit)
Pressure control solenoid D sticking from debris or wear
Wrong fluid level or degraded fluid
Wiring or connector fault on the valve circuit

P2714.d: P2714 says the clutch served by solenoid D does not apply as commanded, so the gearbox slips in a gear that needs it. In GM's 2016 table 16OBDG03 valve D is clutch 4 (C2-3-4-6-8) on the eight-speed and the 2-6 brake on the T76 six-speed; slip of 400 rpm or more for 3 s, counted over three events, sets it after one trip.
s: Slipping or flare in gears that use the affected clutch
No reverse or no forward drive in some cases
MIL lit and transmission in a substitute mode
c: Leaking clutch piston seal or damaged clutch housing (GM 10L1000 C4)
Regulator or line pressure valve stuck by debris or sediment
Internal mechanical failure such as a dislodged retainer ring (GM 10L80)
Low fluid level reducing apply pressure

P2715.d: With P2715 the opposite of P2714 has happened: the clutch fed by valve D keeps holding although the controller wants it released, so it drags into the next gear. GM checks this on its eight-speed through torque-phase and inertia-phase tests on clutch 4, and its 2018 table 18OBDG04 links the code on the nine-speed to C4 exhaust delay times (Type A).
s: Harsh shift or binding as two clutches overlap
Vehicle feels braked when pulling away
MIL lit, transmission may hold a safe gear
c: Debris holding a valve in the applied position
Solenoid D or redundant shutdown valve mechanically stuck
False detection during a stability-control fail-safe (Subaru CVT)
Faulty TCM/solenoid assembly (GM 2-mode hybrid date codes)

P2716.d: P2716 is the general electrical code for pressure control solenoid D: the output stage sees a wrong current or voltage on the coil, without saying whether the circuit is open, grounded or shorted to supply. No manufacturer documents P2716 publicly.
s: MIL lit and transmission in fail-safe mode
Fixed gear or missing gears
Harsh engagement after start
c: Open or shorted coil in solenoid D
Loose, corroded or not fully seated connector
Faulty driver stage in the TCM

P2717.d: P2717 reports that the circuit or response of solenoid D drops out briefly and then comes back. Unlike a hard open or short, the fault is gone by the time the vehicle reaches the workshop, so a static measurement often looks fine.
s: Occasional harsh or flared shift
MIL that comes and goes
No fault found during a workshop check
c: Spread or loose terminal at transmission or TCM connector
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

P2718.d: P2718 points to an open control circuit of solenoid D: the coil draws no current because a wire, pin or the winding itself is broken. GM's 2016 eight-speed table runs the open check on the clutch 4 valve and fails it after 0.3 s within a 0.5 s window (one trip); the 2017 and 2018 nine-speed tables use an impedance measurement.
s: Limp-home mode with limited forward gears
MIL on immediately
Harsh engagements
c: Valve body solenoid connector not fully seated (GM 8L45/8L90)
Broken wire or pushed-out pin in the harness

P2719.d: P2719 means the electrical readings on the control circuit of solenoid D are implausible, although neither a clear open nor a clear short is present. In GM's 2016 table 16OBDG03 the T76 six-speed flags it when the hardware layer reports an invalid voltage in at least 4.4 of 5 seconds; valve D is the 2-6 brake there, and the code is listed without MIL.
s: Stored history code without noticeable symptoms
No MIL on GM vehicles (Type C)
Occasional shift quality changes if the fault is real
c: False history code near freezing fluid temperature in Park/Neutral (GM 6T70/6T75)
High resistance at a terminal or splice

P271A.d: With park-by-wire the pawl is moved by an actuator instead of a cable, and a position sensor tells the controller whether it is engaged. P271A means the signal of sensor A has dropped below its valid band.
s: Vehicle cannot be shifted out of Park
Unexpected shift to Neutral while driving
Service warning such as Shifting System Error
c: Corrosion on the park module circuit board (Ford HF55, recall 26V688)
Sensor A signal wire shorted to ground
Missing or low reference voltage to sensor A

P271B.d: P271B is the upper-limit partner of P271A: the signal from park pawl position sensor A reads above its plausible range. Typical electrical causes are a broken ground or signal wire, which lets the input float towards the reference, or a short to a supply line.
s: Shift system warning on the display
Park cannot be selected or released
c: Open sensor ground or signal wire
Signal wire shorted to reference or battery voltage
Corroded or loose connector at the park actuator

P271C.d: P271C covers the second park pawl position sensor, B, whose signal has fallen below the valid range. Park-by-wire designs often fit two position signals so that a single faulty reading cannot release or engage the pawl by itself; sensor B is the backup or comparison channel to sensor A.
s: Shift system warning, vehicle usually still drivable
Delayed or refused Park engagement
c: Sensor B signal wire shorted to ground
Reference voltage to sensor B missing or low
Corrosion inside the park actuator module

P271D.d: P271D is logged when the signal of park pawl position sensor B sits above its upper limit. Electrically this is the mirror image of P271C: an interrupted sensor ground, an open signal line pulled up inside the controller, or contact with a supply wire.
s: Shift system warning on the display
Park function restricted
c: Open ground or signal wire of sensor B
Signal shorted to a voltage source
Moisture or corrosion in the actuator connector

P271E.d: P271E is a broad performance code for the transmission as a whole, used when the controller finds that the gearbox does not deliver what it should even though no single sensor or valve has failed. Honda applies it to the CVT of the 2016-2020 HR-V: service bulletin A21-046 adds P271E with new PCM software that detects early slip of the primary drive belt.
s: Flashing D indicator and MIL on
Reduced engine power
Engine flare or weak acceleration
c: Slipping or deteriorating CVT drive belt (Honda HR-V)
Insufficient clamping or line pressure in the transmission
Control software without the latest calibration

P271F.d: P271F tells the technician that the controller of an electronically actuated gear shift lacks valid learned positions, so it cannot place the shift elements precisely. Automated and dual-clutch gearboxes store the end and engagement points of their actuators; after replacing a control unit or mechanical parts, or after the stored values are lost, these must be learned again with a scan tool or during a defined drive.
s: Gearbox warning, gear selection limited or blocked
Rough or imprecise engagement
Code returns until a successful learn
c: Learn procedure not run after replacing the control unit or transmission parts
Learn procedure aborted (conditions not met, low battery voltage)
Learned values lost after a software update or power interruption
Actuator or position sensor fault preventing a successful learn

P2720.d: P2720 reports a low signal on the control line of solenoid D, which in practice is a short to ground. GM's 2016 eight-speed table sets it on the clutch 4 valve after a 0.3 s ground-short flag within one trip; the six-speed tables do the same for their valve D.
s: MIL on and limp-home operation
Limited forward gears
Harsh shifts
c: Control wire pinched or chafed against ground
Valve body connector not fully seated

P2721.d: P2721 is logged when the control line of solenoid D reads too high, typically because it touches battery positive. GM's 2016 six-speed tables describe it as circuit high covering an open or a short to power, set after 0.3 s in one trip, so on those units an open line can land here too.
s: MIL on and fail-safe operation
Shift shock or missing gears
Fault may follow wet weather or washing
c: Moisture in the control valve connector (Subaru TR580)
Control wire shorted to a supply circuit
Open circuit on units that report it as high (GM six-speed)
Faulty solenoid D or TCM driver

P2722.d: P2722 is the base code for pressure control solenoid E and leaves the type of fault open. No manufacturer documents P2722 publicly.
s: MIL lit with possible further transmission codes
Irregular shifting or fail-safe gear
Engagement delay into drive or reverse
c: Wiring or connector problem on the solenoid E circuit

P2723.d: P2723 means valve E fails to build the pressure its clutch needs, so that element slips or does not engage. GM's eight-speed table ties E to clutch 5 (C4-5-6-7-8-R) and sets the code after 400 rpm of slip lasting 3 s.
s: Delayed, intermittent or no reverse
Slip or flare in affected gears
MIL on and range inhibit or fail-safe mode
c: Blocked feed orifice in the separator plate (foreign material, GM Allison 1000)
Low fluid level or pump losing prime, especially on cold starts
Solenoid E or its regulator valve sticking
Worn clutch seals leaking apply pressure

P2724.d: P2724 flags valve E as delivering pressure when it should not, so its clutch stays engaged too long. On the Allison 1000 GM watches the off-going element during shifts: an accumulated fail time of 0.3 s on upshifts, 0.5 s on closed-throttle downshifts or 3 s on direction changes counts as stuck on (Type A).
s: Wheels lock or vehicle stops abruptly at low speed
Tie-up or harsh shift feel
MIL on, transmission may hold a safe gear
c: Valve or regulator held in the applied position by debris

P2725.d: P2725 covers an unspecified electrical fault of pressure control solenoid E. The driver notices a coil current or voltage that does not fit the command but does not classify it further.
s: MIL lit and default gear
Firm shifts from fallback pressure
Code returns at once if the fault is permanent
c: Damaged wiring between TCM and solenoid

P2726.d: P2726 describes a fault on solenoid E that is there one moment and gone the next. The controller has seen short drop-outs in the circuit or in the valve's response, not a lasting failure, which makes the code hard to reproduce.
s: Sporadic harsh shift or brief fail-safe
MIL that switches on and off
No fault visible at standstill
c: Harness damaged by engine movement or heat
Water or corrosion in the plug

P2727.d: P2727 is set when the control circuit of solenoid E is open, so no current can flow through the coil. GM's eight-speed table checks the clutch 5 valve for an open-circuit flag over 0.3 s, and on the Allison 1000 the test on PCS 1 is rated Type A.
s: MIL on and limp-home gear
Rear wheels may lock at low speed (GM 8L90 case)
Harsh or missing shifts

P2728.d: P2728 marks the circuit of solenoid E as working but not plausible. GM uses it in two ways.
s: MIL on Allison-equipped trucks
History code without symptoms on GM six-speeds
Firm shifts if pressure control is degraded
c: Coil current deviating from command (resistance change, poor contact)
False history code near 0 °C fluid temperature (GM 6T70/6T75)
Unstable supply voltage to the TCM

P2729.d: P2729 indicates the control line of solenoid E is pulled low, usually by a short to ground. On the Allison 1000 GM detects this when the output connection has almost no impedance to ground and confirms it within 75 ms (Type A).
s: MIL on and fail-safe mode
Abrupt stop or wheel lock at low speed in the GM 8L90 case
Limited gear selection

P272A.d: P272A refers to the control circuit of the electric motor that moves the gearbox into the selected range in shift-by-wire designs. Mitsubishi documents it for the 2022 Outlander with CVT: the shift actuator has two three-phase windings fed through separate relays, and motor A is the one reported as range select motor.
s: MIL and shift warning, often no change in driving
Gear selection refused, vehicle in neutral (second fault)
c: Shift actuator relay A open or stuck off
Open U, V or W phase wire to motor A
Faulty motor coil A in the shift actuator

P272B.d: P272B flags excessive current in the circuit of the range select motor, normally caused by a winding or wire shorted to supply. On the 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander with CVT, Mitsubishi checks this with ignition on: when one of the two phases that should be energised shows the non-energised voltage level (9-16 V instead of about 0 V), the code is set.
s: Vehicle stays in neutral, no gear can be selected
MIL and shift system warning
c: Motor coil A or B phase shorted to power
Damaged harness between shift module and actuator

P272C.d: P272C concerns the control circuit of the motor that engages and releases the park pawl. In the shift actuator of the 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander with CVT this is winding B, powered through its own relay B, while winding A is reported under P272A.
s: MIL on, Park still works normally
Shifting blocked if the other circuit also fails
c: Shift actuator relay B open or stuck off
Open phase wire to motor coil B
Faulty motor coil B in the actuator

P272D.d: P272D reports overcurrent in the park pawl motor circuit, the counterpart of P272B for the second winding. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander CVT service data sets it with ignition on when one of two phases of motor B that ought to carry current sits at the idle voltage level instead of near 0 V, the pattern of a line shorted to supply.
s: Shifting locked out, vehicle held in neutral
MIL and shift warning lamp on
Park may not engage fully
c: Motor coil B or A phase shorted to power
Chafed harness at the shift actuator

P2730.d: P2730 is stored when the control line of solenoid E sits too high, pointing to contact with a supply voltage. GM's Allison 1000 logic looks for a power short at the PCS 1 output and treats it as Type A.
s: MIL on and transmission in fail-safe
Harsh or missing shifts
Code sets again immediately after clearing
c: Control wire chafed against a supply circuit
Open line on units that report it as high (GM six-speed)

P2731.d: P2731 is the parent code for pressure control solenoid F; the standard title names the valve without the kind of fault. GM gives it a concrete job on its nine-speed (GF9) units, where valve F feeds the C6 clutch and the selectable one-way clutch.
s: Hesitation or weak acceleration from low speed
Tie-up feel on the 1-2 shift or stuck in first gear
MIL on, sometimes only intermittently
c: Selectable one-way clutch releasing too slowly
Solenoid F or its regulator valve sticking

P2732.d: P2732 says that the clutch behind valve F does not take up torque although the solenoid works electrically, so the gearbox slips wherever that clutch is needed. On GM nine-speed units valve F serves clutch C6; the TCM counts a failure when C6 slip stays at 200 rpm or more for 3 s, and three such events give a Type A fault after one trip (tables 18OBDG04 and 20OBDG03A).
s: No reverse
Transmission will not shift beyond third gear
Slip or flare and MIL on
c: Mis-stamped spacer plate or worn check ball in the valve body (GM 10L80)
Worn clutch piston seal losing apply pressure (GM 10L1000)
Solenoid F or regulator valve sticking closed
Low fluid level or aerated fluid

P2733.d: P2733 is the reverse case of P2732: valve F keeps pressure on its clutch after the TCM has commanded it off, so the off-going element still carries torque during the shift. GM checks this on its nine-speed units by watching C6 slip while shifting.
s: Tie-up or bind-up feel during shifts
Harsh shifts or engine flare
MIL on and fail-safe gear
c: Solenoid F held open mechanically (solenoid body)
Debris holding the regulator valve in the apply position

P2734.d: P2734 is the catch-all electrical code for solenoid F: the driver stage notices coil current or voltage at odds with the command, without saying whether the line is broken, touching ground or touching battery voltage. Public documentation of P2734 by any maker is lacking.
s: MIL on with limp-home mode
Harsh, late or missing shifts
c: Corroded, loose or damaged connector at the valve body
Chafed or broken wire in the solenoid F circuit
Faulty output stage in the TCM

P2735.d: By its standard title P2735 reports that solenoid F or its circuit fails only now and then, so a static check in the workshop often finds nothing. GM uses the code differently on the dual-clutch gearbox of the 2023 and 2024 Corvette: there valve F is the clutch cooling valve, and P2735 stands for a stuck lube valve.
s: Often no noticeable symptom, code stored without MIL (GM)
Occasional harsh shift or clutch judder
Clutch overheating warning after hard driving
c: Clutch cooling/lube valve sticking (GM Corvette dual-clutch)
Loose or corroded connector causing dropouts
Harness chafing that opens under vibration

P2736.d: P2736 points to an open control circuit on solenoid F, meaning the coil path is interrupted. GM documents the code for several gearboxes.
s: MIL on and limp-home mode
Firm shifts from maximum line pressure or missing gears
c: Valve body connector not fully seated

P2737.d: The standard title describes implausible readings on the control circuit of solenoid F that are neither a clean open nor a short. GM's 2025 table 25OBDG03A fills the code with a hydraulic test on its CVT, where valve F switches the binary oil pump between half and full capacity.
s: MIL on after two trips
Belt slip, flare or reduced power
Whine from the CVT
c: Binary pump control valve sticking (GM CVT)
Primary or secondary pulley pressure sensor reading wrong
High resistance in the solenoid F circuit

P2738.d: P2738 reports a control line on solenoid F that reads too low, which in practice means a short to ground. In GM's 2025 table 25OBDG03A an impedance below 0.5 Ohm between the signal and controller ground, lasting 0.3 s inside a 0.5 s sampling period, is a Type A fault in one trip; the valve there controls a clutch on the nine- or ten-speed, line pressure on the eight-speed or the CVT binary pump.
s: MIL on and fail-safe gear
Harsh engagements or clutch drag
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Fluid or metal debris bridging connector pins

P2739.d: P2739 appears when solenoid F's control line sits too high, usually because it touches battery voltage. GM reacts faster here than for the low case: 25OBDG03A needs only 0.06 s within 0.13 s before the Type A fault is set.
s: MIL on and limp-home mode
Shifts missing or valve function lost
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Short between two solenoid lines in the harness or connector

P273A.d: P273A carries the apply-time test of P2700 to P2705 on to a seventh shift element, G. The controller measures how long element G needs from command to full engagement and stores the code if this time is implausibly long or short.
s: Engine flare or harsh shift into gears using element G
MIL lit, possibly with ratio codes
Fail-safe gear operation
c: Leaking piston seals in the apply circuit of element G
Pressure control or shift solenoid feeding element G sticking
Worn plates or wrong clearance of element G
Adaptive shift values out of range after repair or software update

P273B.d: P273B is the apply-time check for an eighth shift element, H, and therefore only applies to gearboxes with at least eight clutches and brakes. The test is the same as for its siblings: the time between command and full engagement is compared with a calibrated window, and a result outside it sets the code.
s: Delayed or harsh shifts involving element H
MIL lit
Transmission in fail-safe mode
c: Pressure loss in the apply circuit of element H (seals, valve body)
Worn friction plates of element H

P273C.d: Gear shift control module A is the electronic selector used where the gearbox is shifted by wire – lever, rotary knob or push buttons – which turns the driver's choice into a message for the transmission control module. P273C means the supply voltage that this module sees, or reports, has fallen below its lower limit.
s: Selector warning, range cannot be changed
Vehicle will not shift out of Park
Gear indicator flickers or goes blank
c: Weak or discharged 12 V battery, voltage dips at start
Corroded fuse contact, feed wire or ground of the selector module
Alternator or DC/DC converter not supplying enough voltage
Internal fault in the gear shift module

P273D.d: P273D is the over-voltage counterpart of P273C: the gear shift control module A, the electronic selector of a by-wire gear selection, registers a supply above its permitted maximum. No manufacturer documents P273D publicly or names the limit.
s: Selector or gearbox warning in the cluster
Range selection blocked
Other over-voltage faults in several modules
c: Jump-start or charger delivering excessive voltage
Selector module misjudging its supply (software or hardware)

P273E.d: P273E is a condition code: the gear shift control module A – the shift-by-wire selector unit – reports that its internal temperature exceeds the safe limit. No manufacturer documents P273E or its threshold publicly.
s: Selector warning, functions limited
Range changes refused until the module cools
c: Internal fault or overloaded output stage in the selector module
High ambient or radiant heat at the module location
Shorted lock solenoid or actuator driven by the module

P273F.d: P273F is a condition code, not a wiring fault: sensor B delivers a valid reading, but that reading lies above the overheating limit the calibration allows. No manufacturer publishes P273F or its threshold.
s: Transmission overheating message
Reduced torque or changed shift pattern
Burnt-smelling or darkened fluid
c: Sustained high load – towing, track use, long climbs
Fluid cooler clogged or cooler valve not opening
Fluid level low or fluid aged
Sensor B reading too hot while still in range

P2740.d: P2740 is the umbrella circuit code for a second transmission fluid temperature sensor, labelled B. The control module supplies the thermistor with a reference voltage and flags an electrical fault when the returned signal leaves its plausible window, without separating short from open.
s: Warning lamp or transmission message
Fluid temperature B shows an implausible fixed value on the scan tool
Cooler or hot-fluid protection works with a substitute value
c: Loose, corroded or damaged connector or lead to sensor B
Sensor B thermistor open or shorted internally
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module

P2741.d: P2741 flags a sensor B signal that is electrically intact but physically impossible or inconsistent. The clearest published test is a rate check: GM's 2023/24 dual-clutch module calls the cooler-outlet reading faulty when its filtered gradient exceeds 700 °C per second, confirmed over five samples, as a Type B code (MIL after two trips).
s: Warning lamp after repeated detection
Fluid temperature B jumps on the scan tool
Temperature-dependent clutch or cooler control restricted
c: Contact resistance or loose pin causing signal jumps
Sensor B thermistor drifting or responding erratically
Fault in a control unit with built-in sensor (e.g. Mitsubishi TC-SST)

P2742.d: P2742 reports that the sensor B signal sits below its valid range, and how low is defined differs by maker. GM's 2023/24 dual-clutch TCM treats a cooler temperature sensor value under 200 mV, with hysteresis, for at least 500 ms as too low, Type B; for the usual NTC thermistor that equals an extremely hot reading or a signal wire shorted to ground.
s: Warning lamp after two trips on GM
Scan tool shows sensor B extremely hot (GM, Ford) or extremely cold (Mitsubishi)
Protective strategy with substitute temperature
c: Signal lead of sensor B chafed through and touching ground
Control unit with built-in sensor faulty (Mitsubishi TC-SST)

P2743.d: P2743 is the counterpart of P2742: the sensor B signal is above its valid range. In GM's 2023/24 dual-clutch TCM the cooler temperature sensor must exceed 4745 mV for 500 ms, Type B; with an NTC thermistor fed from 5 V that points to a broken wire, an unplugged connector or a short to supply voltage, and the reading looks extremely cold.
s: Warning lamp or transmission message
Scan tool shows sensor B extremely cold (GM, Ford) or extremely hot (Mitsubishi)
Cooler control falls back on sensor A
c: Open circuit – broken lead or unplugged connector at sensor B
Signal lead shorted to a voltage source
CAN fault or control unit with built-in sensor (Mitsubishi TC-SST)

P2744.d: P2744 covers brief dropouts or jumps in the sensor B signal that do not last long enough for the steady low or high codes. No manufacturer documents P2744 publicly; the makers that do use sensor B (GM and Ford dual-clutch units, Mitsubishi Twin Clutch SST) file erratic readings under P2741 instead.
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Short spikes in fluid temperature B on the scan tool
c: Loose or spread terminal in the transmission connector
Harness to sensor B chafing on hot or moving parts
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

P2745.d: P2745 is the general circuit code for a second intermediate shaft speed sensor, called B. Such a sensor reads a shaft that turns between input and output, on a dual-clutch box typically the second clutch shaft.
s: Check engine light and transmission warning
Harsh or delayed shifts
Limp-home mode with a fixed gear
c: Signal or supply lead to sensor B broken or chafed to ground
Corroded or loose pins at the transmission connector
Internal fault of intermediate shaft speed sensor B
Faulty sensor input in the transmission control module

P2746.d: P2746 means the sensor B signal exists but does not make sense. GM's 2023/24 dual-clutch TCM uses it for the clutch 2 speed sensor: with that clutch fully closed and no microslip, its speed must equal engine speed, and a gap of 150 rpm or more for 1.1 s sets the code; further tests compare it with the speed derived from the output shaft and watch synchronizer speed during gear engagement (above 200 rpm for 50 ms).
s: Check engine light, often immediately
Jerky clutch engagement or erratic shifts
Limp-home mode or one half of the gearbox disabled
c: Metal debris on the sensor tip or incorrect air gap to the reluctor
Interference or poor shielding causing signal spikes
Slipping clutch making the speed comparison fail
Damaged or loose reluctor ring on the shaft

P2747.d: P2747 is meant for the case where sensor B stays silent although the car is clearly moving. No manufacturer documents P2747 publicly.
s: Warning lamp and transmission message while driving
Limp-home mode, often stuck in one gear
Rough or missing upshifts
c: Sensor B failed internally and delivers no pulses
Open supply or signal wire, unplugged connector
Reluctor ring displaced or sensor not seated in its bore

P2748.d: P2748 records short interruptions in the sensor B circuit that heal before a permanent fault can be confirmed. Ford is the one maker that documents it: in the 2024 OBD summary, P2748 is the intermittent check of intermediate shaft sensor B on its ten-speed automatics, run continuously alongside the circuit code P2745 and the plausibility code P2746 within a 30 s monitoring window.
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Occasional harsh shift or shift flare
c: Terminal with weak contact pressure in the sensor or gearbox connector
Harness rubbing through and touching ground intermittently
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

P2749.d: P2749 covers an electrical fault in the circuit of a third intermediate shaft speed sensor, C. No manufacturer documents P2749 publicly, and it is unclear which transmission carries three such sensors: Ford's ten-speeds stop at B, and dual-clutch units have only two clutch shafts.
s: Check engine light
Harsh shifts or limp-home mode
c: Open or grounded wire between module and sensor C

P274A.d: P274A is the general circuit code for a third transmission fluid temperature sensor, labelled C. Few gearboxes carry three fluid sensors, and no manufacturer publicly documents which measuring point C stands for or what limits apply to P274A.
s: Warning lamp
Implausible value for temperature C on the scan tool
Restricted adaptation or protection functions
c: Connector or lead to sensor C damaged or corroded

P274B.d: P274B means the sensor C signal is within electrical limits but does not fit the other information, for example because it barely changes while the gearbox warms or contradicts the other temperature values. The only public manufacturer reference is Ford bulletin 20-2044: 2020 Super Duty trucks with the 6.7 L diesel, built up to 5 February 2020, could light the MIL with P274B, often together with P203B and P2201, pure
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Temperature C stays nearly constant while driving
c: PCM software (Ford 2020 Super Duty 6.7 L, TSB 20-2044)
Sensor C drifting or slow to respond
Added resistance in connector or lead

P274C.d: P274C indicates that the sensor C signal has fallen below the lowest value the module accepts. With the negative-temperature-coefficient thermistors normally used for fluid temperature, a low voltage corresponds to very hot fluid, so the usual culprit is a signal lead touching ground or a sensor with an internal short; real heat rarely drives the reading that far.
s: Warning lamp
Temperature C shows an extremely hot value
c: Signal lead of sensor C shorted to ground

P274D.d: P274D is set when the sensor C signal climbs above its highest permitted value. On a thermistor supplied with 5 V via a resistor, that happens when the circuit opens – a broken wire, a corroded or unplugged connector – or when the signal line touches a voltage source; the display would then show fluid colder than any real climate produces.
s: Warning lamp
Temperature C shows an extremely cold value
Late converter lock-up or cautious shifting
c: Open circuit in sensor C lead or connector

P274E.d: P274E stands for an unsteady sensor C signal: short interruptions or spikes that recover before a permanent low or high fault can mature. No manufacturer publishes this code or its debounce logic.
s: Intermittent warning lamp
Temperature C drops out briefly on the scan tool
c: Harness rubbing on the transmission case

P274F.d: P274F means sensor C reports a plausible value that is nevertheless above the overheat limit set in the calibration. It is a condition report rather than a circuit defect, and no manufacturer documents its threshold or the location of sensor C publicly.
s: Overheating warning
Limited torque or altered shifting
c: High load or heavy clutch slip
Restricted oil flow or clogged cooler
Sensor C reading too hot within range

P2750.d: P2750 says that sensor C produces pulses whose speed is implausible – it disagrees with what the engaged gear and the other shaft speeds predict, jumps too fast or carries noise. No manufacturer documents P2750 publicly.
s: Check engine light after driving
Erratic shift points or flare between gears
c: Metal particles on the sensor tip distorting the signal
Electrical interference on the signal lead
Internal clutch slip making the speeds disagree

P2751.d: P2751 is reserved for a sensor C that sends no pulses at all while the vehicle is demonstrably under way. No manufacturer documents P2751 publicly.
s: Warning lamp during the drive
Limp-home gear or missing shifts
c: Reluctor missing, loose or too far from the sensor

P2752.d: P2752 flags a sensor C circuit that cuts out now and then, briefly enough that neither the circuit code P2749 nor the no-signal code P2751 matures. No manufacturer documents P2752 publicly.
s: Sporadic warning lamp
Occasional rough shift
c: Insulation worn through at a bracket or edge

P2753.d: P2753 is set when the control module finds no closed circuit to the actuator that regulates transmission fluid cooling, usually an electrically switched coolant valve that opens or shuts the flow of engine coolant through the fluid heat exchanger. With the valve output open, the module cannot steer warm-up or cooling of the gearbox oil.
s: Check engine lamp on
Transmission fluid warms up slowly or runs hot when towing
Transmission overheat warning in severe cases
c: Open coil in the transmission fluid cooling valve
Loose or corroded connector at the valve, often after coolant contact
Broken control wire between module and valve
Faulty output stage in the control module

P2754.d: P2754 reports that the drive line to the transmission fluid cooling actuator sits at too low a voltage, which in practice means a short to ground or a heavily loaded output. The module then cannot switch the coolant valve or cooler control as intended, and depending on design the valve may remain permanently open or closed.
s: Check engine lamp on
Fluid temperature higher or lower than normal for the conditions
Usually no change in shift behaviour
c: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Water or coolant in the valve connector
Shorted turns in the valve coil

P2755.d: With P2755 the module sees a high level on the cooler actuator line at a moment when its driver should pull it down, the signature of a short to battery voltage or of a low-side driver that no longer switches. The cooling valve then either cannot be activated or stays energised all the time.
s: Check engine lamp on
Cooling valve permanently on or off
Slower warm-up of the transmission in cold weather
c: Control wire shorted to a battery-voltage line
Valve internally shorted to its supply terminal
Module output transistor no longer switching

P2756.d: P2756 is the base code for the solenoid that meters apply pressure to the torque converter clutch. On its own it names only the component; in UDS-based systems a failure-type byte says what went wrong.
s: Converter lockup missing or unstable
Higher engine speed and fuel use at steady speed
Whine noise or harsh shifts (Toyota 8-speed)
c: Internal transmission damage or debris in the valve body (Toyota 8-speed)
Lockup pressure solenoid sticking or worn
Wiring or connector fault on the solenoid circuit

P2757.d: P2757 means the converter clutch was commanded to apply, yet the speed difference between engine and turbine stayed too large, so the lockup never really happened. It is a functional verdict: the circuit may be electrically sound while the valve, the hydraulic feed or the clutch lining fails to deliver.
s: Engine speed stays high at steady cruise
Higher fuel consumption
Transmission fluid runs hot
Check engine lamp on
c: Sticking lockup solenoid or valve body (Toyota CVT solenoid SL)
Internal converter fault such as a dislodged snap ring (Ram AS69RC)

P2758.d: P2758 is the opposite of P2757: the converter clutch stays engaged although the module has asked it to release. Ford detects it when slip remains below 20 rpm while the release command is active and input torque is above 60 Nm, and the fault has to show up in more than one gear.
s: Engine stalls or nearly stalls when coming to a stop
Shudder or jolt when selecting a gear
Warning lamp depends on manufacturer (Ford none, Mitsubishi MIL)
c: Lockup pressure valve stuck in the apply position
Debris or varnish in the valve body

P2759.d: P2759 is a general electrical fault on the control circuit of the converter clutch pressure solenoid, used where a module cannot distinguish an open from a ground or supply short. No manufacturer documents P2759 publicly.
s: No converter lockup
Slightly higher fuel consumption
Warning lamp on
c: Damaged wire or connector between TCM and solenoid

P275A.d: P275A flags an electrical fault in the circuit of transmission fluid temperature sensor D, the fourth position in the SAE lettering. A gearbox with four separate fluid temperature inputs is rare, and no manufacturer publicly assigns sensor D or describes when P275A is stored.
s: Warning lamp
Temperature D missing or implausible on the scan tool
c: Fault in connector or lead of sensor D

P275B.d: P275B is the rationality code for sensor D: the circuit is electrically sound, yet the value does not behave like real fluid temperature. Published tests on other fluid sensors show what modules look for – a warm-up check (GM's 2025 TCMs expect the main sensor to pass 15 °C within a calibrated time), a stuck-value check and a rate check against impossible jumps, such as Mitsubishi's rejection of 10 °C changes within
s: Warning lamp after repeated detection
Temperature D lags behind or deviates from the other readings
c: Sensor D thermistor aged or slow
Sludge or deposits on the sensor tip

P275C.d: P275C reports that sensor D delivers less signal than the module considers possible. Read against an NTC thermistor this means a reading far hotter than the fluid could be, which almost always points to a pinched or melted lead touching ground, or to a short inside the sensor body.
s: Warning lamp
Temperature D shows an impossibly hot value
c: Pinched or melted lead of sensor D touching ground

P275D.d: P275D is stored when the sensor D signal rises past the top of its window. With a thermistor on a pull-up resistor the voltage climbs towards the supply when current can no longer flow, so an interrupted lead, a pushed-back terminal or an unplugged connector is the usual explanation, followed by a short to a voltage source.
s: Warning lamp
Temperature D shows an extremely cold value
c: Interrupted lead or pushed-back terminal at sensor D
Signal lead shorted to a voltage source

P275E.d: P275E marks an intermittent sensor D circuit: the value drops out or spikes for moments and then returns, too briefly for P275C or P275D. Public manufacturer documentation for this code is lacking; the closest published counterpart is the main sensor's P0714, which Ford's 2012 strategy names among its fluid temperature checks.
s: Warning lamp that appears sporadically
Dropouts of temperature D in a data log
c: Heat-damaged lead that fails when hot
Sensor D with an internal loose connection

P275F.d: P275F is the overheating condition for sensor D: the reading is valid and above the calibrated limit. No manufacturer documents the code, the limit or where sensor D sits.
s: Overheating warning or message
Changed shifting or reduced power
Dark or burnt-smelling fluid
c: Heavy trailer or long steep climbs
Cooler blocked or not keeping up

P2760.d: P2760 records a converter clutch control circuit that drops out now and then and recovers by itself. Ford names it in its 2024 OBD summary as the circuit-intermittent result of the TCC solenoid, written as P0740 with failure byte 1F; its electrical check compares the driver feedback with the commanded state and reacts when they disagree for 1.5 seconds.
s: Lockup drops out briefly, felt as an rpm flare
Fault not reproducible in the workshop
Warning lamp may come and go
c: Loose or spread terminal at the case connector
Wire chafing intermittently against a bracket

P2761.d: P2761 says the TCM has lost continuity to the converter clutch pressure solenoid. GM documents the check in its six-speed TCM tables (16OBDG08 for the MW7 unit in Silverado/Sierra, 18OBDG04 for the T87A): with the driver switched off, an impedance of 173 kΩ or more counts as open, while 9.6 kΩ or less does not; after three hardware counts an intrusive test opens the low-side driver, and two confirming counts set the
s: No torque converter lockup
MIL on after two trips (GM Type B)
Higher cruise rpm and fuel use
c: Broken wire or backed-out pin to the solenoid
Internal controller fault (Ram 6.7 l ECM capacitor leak)

P2762.d: P2762 covers a solenoid circuit that is neither open nor shorted but does not behave as commanded. In GM's six-speed TCM tables for the MW7 (2016) and T87A (2018) the module compares desired with measured solenoid current; a gap of 0.5 A or more in at least 40 of fewer than 80 samples sets the code as Type B, with battery voltage above 10 V.
s: Harsh or slipping converter lockup
Shudder at light throttle in higher gears
Warning lamp depending on application (GM T76 none)
c: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
Weak supply voltage or poor ground at the TCM
Current sensing fault inside the TCM

P2763.d: P2763 means the control circuit of the lockup pressure solenoid reads high. GM's 2018 T87A table treats it as a short to power, at 1.16 Ω or less to a voltage source while the driver is on, Type B.
s: No converter lockup, higher cruise rpm
Transmission warning and MIL
Other solenoid high codes at the same time (Subaru)
c: Moisture in the valve-body connector (Subaru TR580)
Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open circuit where the maker includes it in this code (GM T76/T54)

P2764.d: P2764 is the low counterpart of P2763: the lockup solenoid circuit is pulled toward ground. GM's 2018 T87A table defines it as 0.01 Ω or less to vehicle ground, checked while the driver is off every 6.25 ms.
s: No lockup and higher fuel consumption
Jerking or slipping (62TE)
MIL after one trip on some GM units
c: Solenoid winding shorted to its housing
Failed torque converter when the solenoid tests good (FCA 62TE)

P2765.d: P2765 is the circuit code of a second input speed sensor, B, and what B measures varies. On Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch box (2012) it is the input shaft 2 sensor for reverse and the even gears, faulted when the TCM hardware detects a circuit failure.
s: Check engine light and gearbox malfunction message
Limp-home mode, sometimes without reverse or even gears
Slow take-off and no torque converter lock-up
c: Moisture or corrosion at the sensor B connector pins
Defective sensor B or integrated sensor module inside the gearbox
Open or shorted wiring between sensor and TCM

P2766.d: P2766 marks a sensor B signal that is present but erratic or implausible. Ford's 2012 strategy applies it to the DPS6 dual-clutch box, where sensor B reads input shaft 2.
s: Check engine light after two drives
Sluggish acceleration, manual mode unavailable
Torque converter lock-up disabled
c: Sensor B fouled with metal debris or not seated firmly
Interference or poor ground on the signal circuit
TCM fault keeping the code stored permanently

P2767.d: P2767 reports that pulses from sensor B are missing. Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch box of 2012 checks input shaft 2 for lack of signal under this code, alongside P2765 for circuit faults and P2766 for erratic readings.
s: Warning lamp and transmission fail-safe
Slow start-off and weak acceleration
Manual shift mode not available
c: Connector or terminal letting go, open signal wire
Sensor B failed with no output

P2768.d: P2768 stands for a sensor B signal that drops out or jumps only now and then. Audi bulletin 2067653/9 (2024) covers 2020–24 A4, A5, A6, A7 and Q5 models with gearboxes built from 15 June 2020 to 30 November 2023: if P276800 is stored as passive/sporadic, alone or with P071800, control unit J217 or, where not sold separately, the mechatronic unit is replaced; an active entry calls for normal guided diagnosis.
s: Gearbox malfunction message, intermittent
Limp mode, loss of power or no reverse gear
Occasional missed up- or downshifts
c: Transmission control unit fault on affected production batches
Loose contact or damaged wire in the sensor B circuit
Electrical noise producing false speed spikes

P2769.d: P2769 reports a low level on the converter clutch circuit, in practice a short to ground. It belongs to the P0740 family for converters with a single TCC solenoid, unlike P2764, which refers to a dedicated pressure control solenoid.
s: No converter lockup
Higher rpm and fuel use at highway speed
Check engine lamp on
c: TCC control wire pinched or chafed to ground
Damaged internal transmission harness or lead frame

P276A.d: P276A means the power feed to the motor of a second electric transmission fluid pump, labelled B, is interrupted. Such pumps keep hydraulic pressure or lubrication alive when the engine-driven pump is idle, for instance during stop-start or in a dual-clutch gearbox.
s: Transmission warning lamp
Stop-start deactivated
Reduced performance or limp mode in some designs
c: Blown fuse in the pump supply
Broken supply wire or relay contact

P276B.d: P276B is set when the supply voltage reaching the motor of auxiliary transmission pump B sags below its lower limit. Audi names this code in bulletin 34-17-25 (revision of September 2017) covering 2017 A4/A5/A6 models and the 2018 Q5 fitted with the 0CJ, 0CK or 0CL twin-clutch gearbox.
s: Rattle noise from under the vehicle (Audi)
Transmission warning lamp
Further pump B codes stored
c: High resistance in supply or ground of the pump
Low system voltage from a weak battery

P276C.d: P276C flags an excessive voltage on the motor supply of auxiliary pump B. Either the circuit is shorted to another powered line, the pump module measures wrongly, or the vehicle charging system itself overshoots.
s: Transmission warning lamp
Pump switched off, stop-start unavailable
Other overvoltage codes if charging is at fault
c: Supply wire shorted to another powered circuit
Faulty measurement in the pump control electronics

P276D.d: P276D is the general current code for the motor of auxiliary transmission pump B: the measured current does not fit the commanded speed or load, without the module saying whether it is too low or too high. The narrower siblings P276E and P276F carry that distinction, and P0C26 is the same check for pump A.
s: Noise from the pump area
Transmission warning lamp
Stop-start or shift quality restricted
c: Worn bearings or binding impeller in pump B
Poor ground or connector resistance at the pump

P276E.d: P276E tells you that the motor of a second electric transmission fluid pump, called B, takes less current than its commanded duty would require. A small draw usually means the motor is not really working: a broken winding, worn brushes, extra resistance in the feed or ground, or an impeller spinning freely because it has no fluid to move.
s: Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Engine stop-start no longer operates
Delayed or harsh drive engagement after an engine restart
c: Worn brushes or open winding in the pump B motor
Corroded connector or high-resistance feed/ground to the pump
Low fluid level so the impeller runs without load
Faulty current measurement in the pump controller or TCM

P276F.d: P276F is stored when the motor of auxiliary pump B pulls more current than the module allows. Excess draw points to a motor that is working too hard or is electrically damaged: a dragging bearing, debris or varnish in the pump, very cold thick fluid, a partially shorted winding or a chafed lead touching ground.
s: Warning lamp with transmission fault message
Stop-start function disabled
Possible whine or rattle from the pump area
c: Dragging bearing or debris inside pump B
Chafed pump lead shorting to ground

P2770.d: P2770 flags a high level on the torque converter clutch circuit, meaning a short to the battery supply on the TCC solenoid or its wiring. Ford documents it in the 2024 OBD summary for the 6R80, 6R140, 10R60/10R80 and the 8F front-drive families: P2770 corresponds to UDS P0740_12, while P0740_13 covers an open line and P2769 (P0740_11) a short to ground.
s: MIL on
No converter lockup, higher rpm at highway speed
Higher fuel consumption and fluid temperature
c: TCC circuit chafed against a powered wire
Damaged or contaminated transmission case connector
Internal short in the TCC solenoid
Faulty TCC output driver in the TCM/PCM

P2771.d: P2771 concerns the input that reports whether the transfer case sits in its low range. GM uses it on 2016 Silverado/Sierra with the MW7 gearbox as a plausibility test in the TCM: if the switch says high range while gear ratio math says low, or the reverse, for at least 0.5 s with fluid between 20 and 130 °C, the Type B code sets.
s: Check engine light, often together with a flashing 4WD indicator
Erratic speedometer or ABS warning when a speed signal is affected
Low range not engaging, or transfer case disengaging under load
c: Loose tone wheel or moving output shaft in the transfer case (GM PIP4966B)
Transfer case shift actuator damaged, e.g. by water through the breather (Toyota Tacoma)
Low-range switch or position encoder defective
Damaged wiring or corroded connector between switch and control module

P2772.d: P2772 flags a low-range switch whose signal is electrically valid but does not fit what the drivetrain is actually doing. No manufacturer documents P2772 publicly.
s: Flashing 4WD indicator or range message on the cluster
Low range refused or engaged only after several attempts
Warning light depending on manufacturer
c: Low-range switch or encoder worn or out of adjustment
Range shift not completed (shift fork, actuator or linkage)
Output or turbine speed signal distorted, so the calculated range is wrong

P2773.d: P2773 is stored when the signal line of the low-range switch stays below its permitted voltage band, typically because it is pulled to ground. No manufacturer documents P2773 publicly.
s: 4WD indicator flashing and warning light on
Low range cannot be selected or is reported permanently
c: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Moisture in shift actuator or connector (Toyota Tacoma breather issue)

P2774.d: P2774 reports that the low-range switch input sits above its valid voltage range. With a pulled-up signal line this usually points to an open circuit, a broken ground at the switch or a short to battery voltage.
s: Warning light and flashing 4WD indicator
Low range not recognised after selection
c: Open signal or ground wire, connector unplugged at the transfer case
Signal wire shorted to battery voltage

P2775.d: P2775 covers an upshift paddle or tip switch whose voltage is electrically possible but belongs to neither of its two legal states. GM's twin-clutch TCM tables for 2023 and 2024 read the plus paddle as an analogue input: pressed should give 2.2–3.52 V, released 3.826–4.744 V.
s: Upshift paddle has no effect, manual mode unavailable
Message on the cluster, normally no check engine light
c: Worn or dirty contacts or drifting coding resistor in the paddle
Added resistance in the clock spring or steering wheel connector
Moisture or spilled liquid in the switch

P2776.d: P2776 means the upshift switch input has dropped below the lowest voltage the module accepts. In GM's 2023 twin-clutch TCM the TAPUP input is supposed to stay above 2.519 V even with the paddle pulled; a lower reading, held for at least 150 ms with battery voltage between 8.75 and 18 V and the engine not cranking, sets P2776 as Type C without MIL.
s: Upshift paddle or tip function inoperative
Manual mode message, no check engine light on GM
c: Signal wire shorted to ground, e.g. in the clock spring area
Liquid in switch or connector creating a leak path to ground

P2777.d: P2777 is the over-voltage counterpart for the upshift switch. GM's 2023 twin-clutch TCM watches the TAPUP input and counts up a timer once it exceeds 4.774 V; after 150 ms above that limit, with supply voltage in the 8.75–18 V band, the code is logged as Type C, so no MIL.
s: Upshift paddle without function
Driver information message about manual shifting
c: Open signal or ground circuit, steering wheel connector loose
Broken track in the clock spring
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source

P2778.d: P2778 is meant for an upshift switch signal that jumps around or drops out briefly instead of staying in one state. No manufacturer documents P2778 publicly.
s: Upshift requests occasionally ignored
Occasional unwanted upshift requests
Fault comes and goes, often depending on steering angle
c: Clock spring track cracked, opening at certain steering angles
Loose terminal or poor crimp in the column or wheel connector
Worn or bouncing contact in the paddle

P2779.d: P2779 is the plausibility fault of the downshift paddle or tip switch. GM's 2023 and 2024 TCM tables for the twin-clutch gearbox define two voltage windows for the minus paddle: 2.2–3.52 V when pulled and 3.826–4.744 V at rest.
s: Downshift paddle inoperative
Manual mode refused, usually no MIL
c: Corroded contacts or drifting coding resistor in the minus paddle
Added resistance in the clock spring
Corrosion in the steering wheel connector

P277A.d: P277A is not an electrical fault. The motor of auxiliary pump B runs, yet the oil it delivers escapes before pressure can build, so the module concludes that the hydraulic path around the pump leaks.
s: Stop-start disabled or rough engine restarts
Delayed drive engagement after standstill
Warning lamp, possibly fluid traces under the gearbox
c: Damaged pump seal or O-ring at the pump mounting
Low transmission fluid level letting the pump draw air
Check valve in the pump circuit not sealing
Worn valve body bores causing internal leakage

P277B.d: P277B concerns the power stage that energises the motor of auxiliary pump B, wherever it sits: inside a separate pump controller or in the transmission module. The stage is switched on, but what comes back – current, speed or a status signal – does not fit the command, so the module rates the driver as implausible rather than reporting a plain open or short.
s: Transmission warning or service message
Stop-start unavailable
Jerky drive-off after engine restarts
c: Failing output stage in the pump controller or TCM
Poor ground or low system voltage at the driver
Pump motor loading the driver abnormally
Loose or corroded pins between driver and pump

P277C.d: P277C means the motor of auxiliary pump B is commanded to turn but stands still or nearly so. Volvo uses it: its technical journal 36774 covers 2024–2027 mild-hybrid S60, S90, V60/V90 Cross Country, XC40, XC60 and XC90 models with the Aisin TG-81SC eight-speed, where the TCM stores P277C07.
s: Transmission warning message in the cluster
Stop-start not working
Shifts too early, too late or erratic
c: Jammed impeller or seized pump bearing
Known hardware issue in early gearboxes (Volvo TG-81SC before the serial break)
Pump lost prime because of low fluid
One-off detection without a real fault

P277D.d: P277D reports that the motor or the integrated electronics of auxiliary pump B have become too hot. Pumps of this kind measure their own temperature and stop before damage occurs; the code records that protective shutdown.
s: Stop-start temporarily unavailable, especially in hot weather
Warning lamp or transmission message
c: Long high-load operation in hot conditions
Mechanical drag raising motor current and heat
Faulty temperature sensing in the pump electronics

P277E.d: P277E reports that a gear on the shaft served by clutch A dropped out of engagement by itself while that clutch was carrying the drive, without any shift being commanded. GM's 2023 TCM tables for its dual-clutch gearbox run this check continuously: if the synchronizer of the driving gear shows a speed difference although the odd-gear clutch slips by less than 50 rpm, and this lasts 1000 ms, the code is stored as Type
s: Sudden loss of drive as if the gearbox had shifted into neutral
Odd gears locked out, limp mode with reduced gear choice
Warning lamp and transmission message in the cluster
c: Worn shift-fork detent or rounded engagement teeth on an odd gear
Shift rod drifting due to internal hydraulic leakage or a weak actuator
Fork end positions not relearned after repair or module replacement
Faulty shaft speed signal making a slip appear at the synchronizer

P277F.d: P277F is the even-gear twin of P277E: the controller has found that a gear carried by the shaft of clutch B lost its engagement on its own while the car was driving through that clutch. The evidence comes from speed sensors, which show the synchronizer of the active gear turning at a different speed even though clutch B is practically locked (GM: slip below 50 rpm, 1 s confirmation, Type A in the 2023 dual-clutch TCM
s: Momentary loss of drive in an even gear
Even gears unavailable, gearbox skips between odd gears
Warning lamp with stored transmission fault
c: Worn detent or engagement teeth on an even gear or its sleeve
Shift rod of the even shaft creeping due to leakage in the hydraulic unit
Wrong or missing fork position learning after repair

P2780.d: P2780 tells you the downshift switch voltage has fallen under its lower limit. GM's twin-clutch TCM (tables 23OBDG07 and 24OBDG07) checks the TAPDN input against 2.519 V; if the signal stays under that mark for 150 ms while the supply is inside 8.75–18 V and the starter is not engaged, P2780 is logged as Type C, no MIL.
s: Downshift paddle has no effect
Manual mode not available, normally no check engine light
c: Signal wire rubbed through or pinched to ground

P2781.d: P2781 sets when the downshift switch input climbs above its upper voltage limit. GM's 2023 dual-clutch TCM tables cap the TAPDN signal at 4.774 V; staying above it for 150 ms produces a Type C entry, no MIL.
s: Downshift paddle not working
Permanent code shown at an emissions inspection although the paddle works (software case)
c: TCM software reporting a false permanent code (2021 Corvette, N212350930)
Open signal or ground circuit, loose connector at the wheel
Broken track in the clock spring

P2782.d: P2782 targets a downshift switch signal that flickers, bounces or vanishes for moments. No manufacturer documents P2782 publicly.
s: Downshift occasionally missed
Sporadic unexpected downshift request
c: Clock spring losing contact at certain steering angles
Loose pin in the steering column connector
Bouncing or worn contact in the minus paddle

P2783.d: P2783 warns that the torque converter is at risk of overheating. Ford's 2012 OBD summary shows one concrete use in its 6F front-drive six-speed.
s: MIL on
Changed shift and lockup behaviour
Transmission overheating, burnt fluid smell
c: TCC control valve stuck in the apply position
Debris or varnish in the valve body
Restricted converter or cooler oil flow

P2784.d: P2784 belongs to transmissions with two input or turbine speed sensors whose readings can be compared. When both are healthy their values agree, or differ only by a known ratio; P2784 is set when they drift apart for longer than the module tolerates while each circuit on its own looks fine.
s: Harsh or erratic shifts
Emergency mode with fixed gear
MIL on
c: Metal debris on a magnetic speed sensor tip
One sensor giving a weak or distorted signal
Damaged tone wheel or excessive air gap
Signal interference from poor shielding or connectors

P2785.d: P2785 indicates that the actuator which opens and closes the clutch has become hotter than the controller allows. In automated manual and dry dual-clutch gearboxes this part is usually an electric motor or an electro-hydraulic unit; creeping, hill starts and stop-and-go traffic make it work hard, and the controller measures or models its temperature to protect windings and electronics.
s: Gearbox warning and request to stop or let the system cool
Reduced engine torque or harsh, delayed take-off
Vehicle may refuse to engage a gear until cooled
c: Long creeping, repeated hill starts or towing in slow traffic
Stiff release bearing or lever forcing high actuator current
Worn actuator motor or blocked actuator pump
Faulty temperature sensing or outdated control software

P2786.d: P2786 is stored when the drive that moves the shift forks inside an automated gearbox runs too hot. Single-clutch automated manuals use electro-mechanical or electro-hydraulic actuators to push the selector across and along the gate, and some dual-clutch designs drive their forks with motors as well.
s: Shifts refused or delayed, gearbox stays in current gear
Transmission warning in the instrument cluster
Gearbox may select neutral and only restart after cooling
c: Very frequent shifting, e.g. manual mode on hilly roads or in traffic
Binding shift fork, selector shaft or linkage raising actuator load
Worn shift actuator motor or low hydraulic pressure in the shift unit
Temperature model or software error in the gearbox controller

P2787.d: P2787 means the controller has calculated or measured a temperature for clutch A above its permitted limit. Two quite different uses are documented.
s: Overheating message, odd gears or all-wheel drive unavailable
MIL or transmission warning lamp on
Shudder or slipping when pulling away
c: Clutch slipping because its actuator or actuator pump does not deliver full force
On all-wheel-drive couplings, damaged front differential forcing constant slip
Repeated launches, creeping or towing with high clutch slip
Worn friction lining reducing torque capacity

P2788.d: P2788 is the system-level code for an automated manual gearbox whose learned correction values have reached the end of their allowed range. Such units learn the clutch bite point, engagement speed and the end stops of the shift and select movements so that gear changes stay smooth as parts wear; when a value would have to move beyond its limit, the controller can no longer compensate and stores this code.
s: Jerky take-off and harsh or slow shifts
Transmission warning lamp
Clutch slip or engine flare during shifts
c: Worn clutch moving the bite point beyond the learnable range
Basic setting or relearn skipped after clutch, actuator or module work
Worn or sticking shift and clutch actuators changing their travel
Outdated software or implausible engine torque signal

P2789.d: P2789 says the controller has pushed its learned fill or pressure corrections for a clutch to the edge of the permitted window and still cannot reach the shift quality it aims for. The code is well documented by Allison for its 1000/2000 Series automatics, where it lights the Check Transmission lamp and the Prognostics view flags the affected clutch as not OK.
s: Check Transmission or warning lamp on
Engine flare or slip during upshifts
Harsh or delayed engagement of the affected clutch
c: Outdated transmission calibration needing a reflash
Engine reports torque inaccurately, so clutch adaptation drifts
Worn clutch plates or leaking clutch piston seals
Degraded fluid or a sluggish pressure control solenoid

P278A.d: P278A is the general circuit fault of the kickdown switch, the contact at the end of accelerator pedal travel that asks the transmission for the lowest possible gear. No manufacturer documents P278A publicly.
s: No forced downshift at full throttle
Reduced acceleration when overtaking
c: Kickdown switch in or under the pedal defective
Wiring or connector of the pedal module damaged
Kickdown message missing on the data bus (networked designs)

P278B.d: P278B describes a kickdown switch whose state contradicts the pedal position. No manufacturer documents P278B publicly.
s: Kickdown missing at the pedal stop
Unexpected downshift at part throttle
c: Kickdown switch misadjusted or detent worn
Floor mat or object preventing full pedal travel
Pedal position sensor offset so that both signals disagree

P278C.d: P278C is recorded when the kickdown switch line reads lower than the module allows. No manufacturer documents P278C publicly, and many modern pedals have no electrical kickdown contact at all, as Mazda notes for the 2024 CX-90.
s: Kickdown always or never active, depending on circuit
Unexpected downshifts or lack of downshift at full throttle
c: Signal wire shorted to ground at the pedal bracket
Water from the footwell in the connector

P278D.d: P278D means the kickdown switch circuit shows a voltage above its permitted maximum. No manufacturer documents P278D publicly.
s: No kickdown at full throttle
Slower acceleration from speed
c: Open signal or ground wire, pedal module unplugged
Signal wire shorted to battery voltage

P278E.d: P278E stands for a kickdown switch signal that drops out or toggles irregularly. No manufacturer documents P278E publicly; the monitoring idea follows CARB's call for circuit checks on inputs, and Eaton's Endurant HD diagnostics show the networked equivalent, where a kickdown message that is invalid or absent for 5 s is logged as fault 167.
s: Kickdown works only sometimes
Fault not reproducible when stationary
c: Bouncing switch contact due to worn detent
Wire strands breaking where the harness flexes with the pedal

P278F.d: P278F flags that the learned values for clutch B have run out of room. In a dual-clutch gearbox this is usually the clutch for the even gears; the controller keeps adjusting its touch point and pressure or travel so that handovers between the two clutches stay seamless, and stores the code once a correction hits its end stop.
s: Shudder or slip when an even gear takes over
Rough or slow shifts between gears
Transmission warning lamp
c: Worn clutch B lining or plates shifting the touch point
Clutch adaptation not reset or relearned after repair
Clutch B actuator or release mechanism sticking or losing pressure
Outdated software or inaccurate engine torque information

P2790.d: P2790 is the basic circuit fault for the signal that tells the controller in which direction the selector mechanism is moving across the gate, that is sideways between the shift lanes of the H pattern. In automated manual gearboxes the select actuator or its sensor provides this information; on some shift-by-wire levers it comes from the lever itself, so the exact part depends on the manufacturer.
s: Gear changes refused or gearbox stuck in one gear
Vehicle may not move off from standstill
Warning lamp with transmission message
c: Open wire or loose, corroded connector at the select sensor
Failed select direction sensor or select actuator electronics
Fault in the shift lever module where it supplies the signal
Defective input stage in the transmission controller

P2791.d: P2791 is set when the gate select direction signal sits below the lowest value the controller accepts. For a voltage-type sensor this usually points to a short to ground on the signal wire, a missing reference supply or a sensor pulling the line down internally; with switch-type inputs the contact may read as permanently closed to ground.
s: No change between shift lanes, limited gear choice
Gearbox holds the current gear or selects neutral
Transmission warning lamp
c: Signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Sensor reference voltage missing or shorted
Select direction sensor failed with low output

P2792.d: P2792 reports a gate select direction signal stuck above its valid band. Common reasons are a short between the signal line and a supply voltage, a broken sensor ground that lets the input float up, or an open signal wire on inputs with an internal pull-up resistor; a sensor with a failed output stage can also hold the line high.
s: Sideways selection blocked, shifts possible only in one lane
Gearbox may stay in gear or neutral
Transmission warning lamp
c: Signal wire shorted to a supply voltage
Broken sensor ground or open signal line pulled up internally
Select direction sensor failed with high output

P2793.d: P2793 covers the circuit that reports the shift direction, the fore-and-aft movement along a lane that actually engages or releases a gear, as opposed to the sideways lane choice monitored by P2790. Depending on the design, an automated manual reads it from a sensor on the shift actuator, while shift-by-wire systems may take it from the lever or a separate selector module.
s: No up- or downshifts, gearbox keeps the current gear
Selector input ignored
Warning lamp and transmission message
c: Open circuit or poor contact at the shift direction sensor connector
Failed shift direction sensor on the actuator
Faulty shift lever or selector module where it sends the signal

P2794.d: P2794 means the shift direction signal, which tells the controller whether a gear is being pushed in or pulled out along its lane, reads lower than the permitted minimum. The usual suspects are a signal line rubbed through to ground, a collapsed sensor supply shared with other sensors, or water in a connector creating a leakage path to ground.
s: Gearbox stays in the current gear
Manual shift requests ignored
Transmission warning lamp
