c: Signal line chafed through to ground
Shared sensor supply pulled down by another sensor or wiring
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

P2795.d: P2795 is the upper-limit fault of the shift direction signal: the value seen by the controller is higher than any real sensor position could produce. That pattern fits a signal wire touching a battery or 5 volt feed, a lost sensor ground, or an interrupted signal line on an input that is pulled up inside the module.
s: Gear changes refused, current gear held
Selector or paddle inputs have no effect
Transmission warning lamp
c: Signal wire shorted to battery or 5 V supply
Lost sensor ground or open signal line pulled up internally
Shift direction sensor stuck at a high output

P2796.d: P2796 points to an interrupted control line between the module and the motor of auxiliary pump A. GM's 2025 TCM tables define the test: provided the battery supplies 9 to 15 V, the controller sees more than 200 kΩ from signal to ground in at least 20 of 25 samples taken every 100 ms; the code is Type B, so the MIL comes on after two trips.
s: MIL or wrench indicator on
Stop-start inoperative
Reduced performance message on electrified models
c: Broken control wire or unplugged pump connector
Poor terminal contact at the pump or module
Open circuit inside the pump electronics

P2797.d: P2797 says pump A was asked to deliver but no useful pressure resulted. GM checks this on CVTs during an engine auto-start: with the pump commanded and over 400 kPa requested at both pulleys, both pressure sensors reading under 200 kPa for more than 0.525 s set the Type B code.
s: MIL on
Stop-start inoperative
Shock or surge when the engine restarts at a stop
Service transmission message
c: Internal failure of the auxiliary pump or its motor
Control software misjudging pump output (TCM update available)
Low fluid or internal leakage preventing pressure build-up

P2798.d: P2798 reports the control circuit of auxiliary pump A pulled low, which in practice means a short to ground. In GM's 2025 TCM tables the controller registers less than 0.5 Ω between the signal and controller ground in 20 of 25 samples at a 100 ms rate, with battery voltage between 9 and 15 V; it is a Type B fault with the MIL after two trips.
s: Reduced propulsion power message on electric vehicles
Service vehicle soon lamp or MIL
Stop-start disabled on combustion models
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Internal defect in the pump electronics (e.g. faulty solder joints, Bolt EV/EUV)
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins in the connector
Faulty control output in the module

P2799.d: P2799 is set when the control line of auxiliary pump A sits at too high a level, normally because it touches a powered wire. GM's 2025 TCM tables are the only public manufacturer description: the module measures under 0.5 Ω from the signal line to a voltage source in 20 of 25 samples spaced 100 ms apart, provided supply voltage is between 9 and 15 V, and treats the result as Type B with the MIL after two trips.
s: MIL after two drive cycles
Stop-start inoperative
Rough engagement after an auto-start
c: Control wire shorted to a powered circuit
Moisture bridging pins in the pump connector
Internal short in the pump electronics
Faulty high-side driver in the module

P279A.d: P279A fires when the transfer case should be in its high range, but the measured ratio says otherwise. GM explains the check in its 2019 ECM tables (section for the LCV engine): the ratio is calculated from transmission output speed divided by transfer case output speed, both from real sensors.
s: MIL and 4WD warning on
Unexpected low-range feel or loss of drive
Grinding from the transfer case
c: Range shift to high not completed by the shift motor
Worn shift fork or range sleeve slipping out of high
Implausible transfer case output speed signal
Mismatched tire sizes affecting the computed ratio

P279B.d: P279B is the reverse case of P279A: 4WD low has been commanded, yet the transfer case behaves like high range or neutral. For a vehicle crawling off-road this is a real safety concern, because the expected reduction and engine braking are missing.
s: No reduction in 4WD low, weak crawling and engine braking
4WD warning lamp and MIL
Clunking or grinding when selecting low range
c: Shift motor stopping short of the low position
Worn or damaged reduction planetary set
Broken or bent range shift fork
Faulty speed signal distorting the ratio

P279C.d: P279C applies when neutral is commanded on the transfer case, as is done for flat towing, but the shafts still turn with a fixed ratio that matches high or low range. The transfer case therefore still transmits drive.
s: Vehicle still drives or creeps with neutral selected
Neutral request rejected, 4WD warning on
MIL on
c: Range shift motor not reaching neutral
Sticking shift sleeve keeping a range engaged
Wrong position feedback from the range sensor

P279D.d: P279D concerns the signal that tells the powertrain which transfer case range is active: 4WD high, 4WD low or neutral. Drivetrain controllers need it to apply the right ratio, torque limits and shift logic.
s: Check engine lamp
4WD range indicator wrong, flashing or unavailable
Range change between high and low refused
c: Range message from the transfer case module corrupted or out of sequence
Open circuit or bad connector on the range switch or sensor
Faulty transfer case control module or range sensor
Software mismatch between the modules after a replacement

P279E.d: P279E flags a 4WD range signal that is electrically present but does not make sense: it may show a range the transfer case cannot be in, jump between high, low and neutral without a request, or contradict what the speed ratio across the transfer case shows. Such a plausibility check typically compares the reported range with commanded shifts and with the measured ratio monitored by P279A to P279C.
s: 4WD indicator shows a range that does not match the actual drive
Range shifts refused or completed only partly
Warning lamp
c: Worn or misadjusted transfer case range sensor
Transfer case shift motor stopping between ranges
Intermittent contact in the range signal wiring

P279F.d: P279F means the wired 4WD range signal is below the lowest valid level. Many transfer cases report their range through a resistor-coded switch or a position sensor that produces a defined voltage for each of high, low and neutral; a reading under the lowest of these bands points to a short to ground, a missing sensor supply or a sensor that pulls the line down.
s: 4WD range indicator dark or flashing
4WD low or range changes unavailable
Warning lamp on
c: Range signal wire shorted to ground near the transfer case
Range switch or encoder failed with low output

P27A0.d: P27A0 is logged when the line reporting which transfer case range is engaged (4WD high, 4WD low, neutral) reads above its highest valid level. Range encoders usually present a defined voltage or resistance band for each position; a value above all bands typically means the wire is open and pulled up inside the module, the encoder lost its ground, or the line touches a battery feed.
s: 4WD indicator flashing or showing no range
Shift between 4WD high and low refused
Warning lamp or driveline message
c: Range signal wire or encoder ground interrupted (corroded or loose connector near the transfer case)
Signal wire chafed against a powered conductor
Transfer case range encoder or switch defective

P27A1.d: P27A1 means auxiliary transmission fluid pump A keeps running although the controller has not asked for it, or the module still sees current or rotation with the command off. Such electric pumps hold pressure in the gearbox while the engine rests during stop-start or hybrid operation.
s: Pump hum from the gearbox after the engine or ignition is off
12 V battery discharged after standing
Stop-start disabled and warning shown
c: High-side driver or pump relay stays closed
Pump control or enable line shorted to battery voltage
Integrated pump electronics ignore the off command

P27A2.d: P27A2 flags a broken control circuit between the module and auxiliary pump B, the second electric fluid pump on gearboxes that carry two. While its output is energised, the controller compares the voltage on the line with the level an intact load would pull it to; a floating line reveals the interruption.
s: Stop-start no longer active
Transmission warning or MIL
Harsh engagement when driving off after a restart
c: Control wire broken in the harness to pump B
Pump connector unplugged, pin pushed back or corroded
Open motor winding or internal connection in pump B

P27A3.d: P27A3 means auxiliary pump B was commanded but did not deliver: no pressure build-up, too little speed or a motor that does not respond at all. Audi documents the code.
s: Rattle from below the car near the gearbox
Stop-start disabled
Delayed or harsh engagement after an engine restart
c: Pump B mechanically defective or seized (e.g. assembly fault on Audi V553)
Fluid level too low, pump draws air
Worn pump motor or high resistance in its supply

P27A4.d: P27A4 indicates that the control line of auxiliary pump B is pulled toward ground. The module checks the line while its driver is switched on; if the measured level stays close to zero, the circuit counts as shorted low.
s: Stop-start unavailable
MIL or transmission warning after repeated trips
Blown fuse in the pump supply possible
c: Control wire insulation chafed through to ground
Water or corrosion bridging pins to ground in the pump connector
Internal short to ground inside pump B

P27A5.d: P27A5 sets when the control line of auxiliary pump B sits at a level that only a connection to a voltage source can explain. In practice the wire touches a powered conductor, or moisture links it to a neighbouring supply pin.
s: Stop-start switched off
Pump B may run continuously or not at all
MIL after two trips on Type B systems
c: Control wire chafed against a powered conductor
Moisture bridging the control pin to a supply pin
Faulty output stage in the controlling module

P27A6.d: P27A6 reports that auxiliary pump B keeps running, or keeps drawing current, while the controller has it switched off. Audi lists P27A600 in bulletin 34-17-25 for 2017 A4, A5 and A6 and 2018 Q5 models with 0CJ, 0CK and 0CL dual-clutch gearboxes; there the code may appear together with a rattle from the gear oil pump V553, which Audi traced to an assembly fault at the supplier and cures with a new pump.
s: Pump noise or rattle from the gearbox area with the engine off
Weak or flat 12 V battery
Transmission warning stored
c: Pump B module or electronics defective (e.g. Audi V553 supplier fault)
Driver output or relay remains closed
Control line shorted to battery voltage

P27A7.d: P27A7 means the transmission controller holds no usable calibration curve for pressure control solenoid A. Each valve body is measured at the factory, and GM writes its current-to-pressure data into TCM memory; at every start-up the module checks that record.
s: MIL on right after start-up
Harsh engagements or firm shifts from imprecise line pressure
Transmission may run a substitute program
c: New or service TCM installed without loading the solenoid characterization data
Valve body replaced but the data for its part number not written to the TCM
Data set for a different solenoid class or valve body entered
Programming aborted, leaving a corrupted block (checksum error)

P27A8.d: With P27A8 the TCM rejects the stored characterization record of pressure control solenoid B. GM's 2016 eight-speed table 16OBDG03 ties B to clutch 2 (CB12345R) and logs the code within one trip when that record is marked as not programmed.
s: MIL illuminated
Converter lock-up shudder or no lock-up on the nine-speed
Uneven upshifts involving the affected clutch
c: Characterization download skipped after TCM or valve body replacement
Data loaded for the wrong valve body part number
TCM non-volatile memory corrupting the stored block

P27A9.d: P27A9 concerns solenoid C. GM's controller compares the calibration it holds for this valve with the valve body actually fitted; if the block for C is absent, of the wrong device class, damaged or non-monotonic, the fault is stored at power-up and lights the MIL in that same trip (Type A in 20OBDG04 and in the 2025 table 25OBDG03A).
s: MIL on in the first drive after the fault
Slipping or harsh application of the clutch fed by valve C
On the CVT, unstable line pressure and belt slip risk
c: Replacement TCM fitted without solenoid C data
Valve body or solenoid assembly swapped without updating the TCM
Stored data corrupted, checksum no longer matches

P27AA.d: P27AA is set when the TCM finds the calibration block for pressure control solenoid D unusable. Which hardware that is depends on the gearbox: GM's 2016 eight-speed assigns D to clutch 4 (C23468), while the 2017-2020 tables put the nine-speed's C2 clutch (CB29), the ten-speed's C5 clutch and the CVT's C1 clutch behind the same letter, so the D used by stuck-off code P2714 is not always the same part.
s: MIL and stored DTC at key-on
Rough shifts into gears using the clutch behind valve D
c: Solenoid data not loaded after a transmission or TCM repair
Used TCM from another vehicle still carrying its old valve body data
Wrong valve body part number used for the download

P27AB.d: Solenoid E's characterization data failing the TCM's plausibility test produces P27AB. In GM's 2018 table 18OBDG04 the record is written at vehicle assembly according to the valve body part number and must be rewritten by the dealer whenever the valve body is serviced; a missing or partial block, a device class mismatch, a checksum error or falling axis values all count as failures (Type A, one trip).
s: MIL lit
Flare or bump on shifts using the clutch behind valve E
On the CVT, irregular torque converter lock-up
c: Valve body serviced without rewriting the solenoid data
Incomplete programming session after TCM replacement
Solenoid class in the data does not match the TCM calibration

P27AC.d: P27AC reports invalid calibration data for pressure control solenoid F. On GM's 2016 eight-speed this is the line pressure solenoid, and the TCM logs the fault in one trip once the data are found unprogrammed.
s: MIL on
Firm or soft shifts throughout when line pressure depends on valve F
Possible fixed-gear substitute mode
c: TCM swapped and solenoid F data never loaded
Remanufactured valve body with a new ID not entered into the TCM
Data block damaged by a voltage drop during programming

P27AD.d: P27AD flags the stored data for pressure control solenoid G as not matching the hardware. GM's 2016 eight-speed table names G the torque converter clutch solenoid and sets the code in one trip.
s: MIL illuminated
Converter clutch or range mode problems, depending on transmission
General shift harshness on ten-speed units
c: Solenoid G data missing after TCM programming
Valve body changed without matching data
TCM calibration for a different transmission variant

P27AE.d: P27AE is the highest letter GM publicly checks for characterization data. It is absent from the 2016 eight-speed table and first appears in 17OBDG04, where H stands for the nine-speed's C6 clutch (C6789) and the ten-speed's torque converter clutch; 20OBDG04 adds mode valve B on CVTs with electronic range select.
s: MIL on
Shudder or missing converter lock-up on ten-speed units
Higher fuel consumption if lock-up is suppressed
c: Replacement TCM delivered blank and not set up with valve body data
Valve body or solenoid service without data update

P27AF.d: No manufacturer documents P27AF publicly. By its wording it would mean that the TCM considers the stored calibration of a ninth pressure control solenoid, letter J, invalid.
s: MIL illuminated
Rough or inconsistent shifts involving the element behind valve J
c: Solenoid data not loaded after TCM or valve body replacement
Data set for another valve body variant
Corrupted calibration block in TCM memory

P27B0.d: P27B0 closes the data-incompatible series with letter K, and no public manufacturer document uses it. It would describe a tenth pressure control solenoid whose calibration record in the transmission controller is missing, mismatched or corrupt.
s: MIL on
Shift quality problems on gears using valve K
c: Valve K data never programmed into a new or used TCM
Valve body ID in the TCM differs from the fitted unit
Software update overwrote or damaged the data block

P27B1.d: P27B1 belongs to a family of codes raised by an independent supervision layer in the transmission or powertrain module. That layer repeats key transmission decisions in parallel and flags the main software when both results disagree, as a guard against unintended vehicle motion.
s: Transmission warning or wrench light
Restricted gear selection or default gear
c: Supervision or main software calibration in the module
Implausible clutch shaft speed or position input
Internal fault in the transmission control module

P27B2.d: P27B2 is set when the monitoring layer cannot confirm that the gearbox is really in the range the main software intends. In GM's 2024 tables for heavy-duty trucks, the TCM checks actual solenoid and pressure switch states with the pattern expected for the range; if they disagree for a full second, the code is logged, lighting the MIL on the first trip.
s: Vehicle stuck in park or will not start
Warning lamp or transmission message
Range change refused
c: Module software (Ford fixes by reprogramming, e.g. TSB 25-2362)
Unusual operating sequence such as selecting a gear after remote start without braking
Solenoid or pressure switch state not matching the commanded range

P27B3.d: P27B3 is the monitoring code for the path that turns a chosen gear into actuator commands. In Ford's wording it supervises the actuator manager.
s: Wrench light or transmission message
Certain gears or engine braking functions blocked
c: Electrical fault at the selectable one-way clutch actuator (Ford 8/10-speed)
Safety-relevant CAN transmit signal faulty (Ford TR9070)

P27B4.d: P27B4 concerns the direction in which the vehicle actually moves compared with the selected gear. GM's 2024 heavy-duty TCM tables compare the direction reported by the output speed sensor with the direction implied by solenoid and pressure switch states; disagreement for one second sets the code with MIL on the first trip.
s: MIL or wrench light
Forced idle or reduced power
Gear engagement blocked until restart
c: Module software strategy (Ford reprograms PCM or SOBDMC)
Faulty direction information from the output speed sensor
Solenoid or pressure switch reporting a state that does not match the gear

P27B5.d: P27B5 sets when the supervision software doubts the ratio the transmission is running. Ford describes two triggers in its 2024 summary for the eight- and ten-speed automatics: protection against overspeeding a driveline element (UDS P0701_B1) and a plausibility test of the shaft speed ratio (P0701_64), both non-MIL; the 2020–2023 edition likewise keeps it without MIL on electronically shifted models.
s: Warning lamp or wrench light
Forced idle or torque reduction
Transmission held in a fixed gear
c: Implausible input, intermediate or output shaft speed signal
Real slip of a clutch producing an unexpected ratio

P27B6.d: P27B6 is the supervision check on the transmission speed signals. GM's 2024 heavy-duty TCM tables work out the output speed that should result from turbine speed and the current gear ratio and set the code, MIL on the first trip, when the raw output speed deviates by 10 or more for at least 10 seconds while output speed is at least 50, the range is not neutral and no shift is under way.
s: MIL or wrench light
Harsh or abrupt deceleration events
Fixed gear or limited shifting
c: Turbine or output speed sensor delivering an implausible signal
Damaged tone wheel or interference on sensor wiring

P27B9.d: P27B9 says pressure control solenoid N does not build hydraulic force when commanded. On dual-clutch gearboxes this letter belongs to the second synchronizer pressure valve: Ford's 2024 summary lists it for SPV2 of the TR9070, and GM's 2023 Corvette table 23OBDG07 calls it shift solenoid 2 hydraulically stuck off.
s: MIL on
Certain gears cannot be selected; gear skipping
Substitute mode with reduced gear set
c: Valve spool sticking closed from debris or varnish
Low or contaminated transmission fluid reducing supply pressure
Leak in the synchronizer actuator circuit
Mechanically binding shift rod or fork

P27BA.d: P27BA is the opposite fault to P27B9: solenoid N keeps applying pressure when it should be released. GM's dual-clutch table 23OBDG07 (Corvette) describes the effect of a synchronizer valve 2 stuck on as a constant push on one shift rod.
s: MIL and transmission warning
Gear clash or grinding on shifts
Limp mode with restricted gears
c: Valve spool stuck open by contamination
Worn solenoid armature not returning to rest
Fluid contaminated with clutch or synchronizer wear particles

P27BB.d: P27BB is a catch-all electrical code for pressure control solenoid N, and no manufacturer documents it publicly. The two makers known to use solenoid N, GM on the Corvette dual-clutch unit (23OBDG07) and Ford on the TR9070, both split electrical faults of this synchronizer valve into separate codes instead: P27BD covers an open load, P27BF a grounded line and P27C0 a line shorted to battery voltage.
s: MIL on
Gears served by solenoid N unavailable
c: Solenoid N coil open or shorted
Corroded or loose internal transmission connector
Damaged harness between TCM and transmission
Faulty output driver in the TCM

P27BC.d: P27BC reports that the signal or response of pressure control solenoid N drops out now and then rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the GM and Ford dual-clutch documents that use solenoid N for the second synchronizer valve (23OBDG07, Ford TR9070 list) only publish its permanent electrical and hydraulic faults.
s: MIL that comes and goes
Occasional missed or delayed shifts
c: Loose or spread terminal at solenoid N or TCM

P27BD.d: P27BD stands for an open control circuit of solenoid N. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table 23OBDG07 names the part synchronizer actuation valve 2 and tests it while its low-side output is switched off: the driver chip tries to hold the pin at a small voltage with a tiny current, which only works without a load connected.
s: MIL on in the same trip
Gears on the affected shift rod blocked
Transmission substitute mode
c: Broken control wire between TCM and solenoid

P27BE.d: P27BE means the control circuit of solenoid N is electrically intact but behaves implausibly, for example a measured current that does not follow the command. No manufacturer documents P27BE publicly.
s: MIL on
Slow or incomplete gear engagement on one shift rod
c: Solenoid N coil resistance out of specification
High resistance at connector or crimp
Unstable supply voltage to the TCM

P27BF.d: P27BF indicates the control line of solenoid N is pulled too low, in practice a short to ground. GM's 23OBDG07 table for the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox checks synchronizer actuation valve 2 while its low-side switch is on: should the sense-pin voltage fall below about 1.7 V (tolerance 0.5 V), the driver chip reports a ground short; 150 ms confirmation, battery between 8.75 and 18 V, engine not cranking, Type A.
s: MIL on immediately
Unintended gear actuation or locked-out gears
Limp mode
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Moisture or corrosion bridging the connector
Solenoid winding shorted to its housing

P27C0.d: P27C0 reports too high a voltage on the control line of solenoid N, usually a short to battery or to a neighbouring output. On the Corvette with GM's dual-clutch gearbox (table 23OBDG07, 2023), synchronizer actuation valve 2 is flagged when the sense voltage stays above roughly 0.7 to 1.1 V, depending on supply voltage, while the low-side switch is on, or when actual current misses the target by over 70 % for 60 ms o
s: MIL on
Shift rod cannot be actuated; gears missing
Code returns at every start after a shutdown test
c: Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Two solenoid lines shorted together in the harness or connector
Partially shorted solenoid coil drawing wrong current
Damaged output stage in the TCM

P27C1.d: P27C1 is logged when pressure control solenoid P is commanded but the shift rods it serves barely move. In GM's Corvette dual-clutch documentation (23OBDG07, unchanged in 24OBDG07) the part is shift solenoid 3; with the selector valve in one position it pushes rod 3, in the other rod 4, both in the A-to-B direction.
s: MIL on with transmission warning
Certain gears skipped or not selectable
Delayed or failed launch in affected gear
c: Valve spool of solenoid P held in the closed position by debris or varnish
Low, aerated or degraded transmission fluid so no pressure builds
Leaking seal on the shift rod actuator piston for rods 3/4
Mechanically binding shift rod or fork

P27C2.d: P27C2 means solenoid P keeps pressurizing after it should have vented. GM's dual-clutch Corvette table 23OBDG07 (and 24OBDG07) detects this on shift solenoid 3 by watching what happens just after the selector valve switches: if one of rods 3 and 4 travels 1,000 µm or more within 200 ms without a command while the other one drops back by at least 125 µm, valve 3 is judged hydraulically stuck on, Type A.
s: MIL on and gears blocked by the controller
Clunk or grinding during gear changes
Unexpected loss of drive (neutral)
c: Spool of solenoid P jammed in the open (pressure-applying) position
Wear particles in the fluid keeping the valve from closing
Worn valve bore letting pressure bypass to the actuator

P27C3.d: P27C3 is the general electrical fault code for pressure control solenoid P. No manufacturer documents it publicly.
s: MIL on
Gears on the affected shift rods unavailable
Transmission in emergency mode
c: Solenoid P winding open or shorted
Damaged or corroded pin in the transmission connector
Chafed or broken lead between solenoid and TCM
Faulty output stage in the TCM

P27C4.d: P27C4 indicates that solenoid P works most of the time but its circuit or response briefly drops out. No manufacturer documents the code publicly; GM's Corvette DCT table 23OBDG07 and Ford's TR9070 list, which both use this solenoid as synchronizer valve 3, only publish hard faults such as P27C5, P27C7, P27C8 and the hydraulic codes P27C1/P27C2.
s: MIL that comes and goes
Occasional harsh or missed shift
c: Wire strand broken inside intact-looking insulation
Solenoid winding that opens at operating temperature

P27C5.d: P27C5 reports an open control circuit on solenoid P. GM's Corvette dual-clutch table 23OBDG07 tests synchronizer actuation valve 3 for this while its low-side driver (a TLE8242 chip) is off: an intact coil pulls the sense pin up towards battery voltage, whereas without a load the driver manages to hold it in a window of about 1.7 to 3.0 V.
s: MIL on immediately
Shifts on rods 3 and 4 in A-to-B direction not possible
Limp mode with restricted gears
c: Connector not latched or pin pushed back
Broken control wire between TCM and solenoid

P27C6.d: P27C6 describes a control circuit for solenoid P that is neither open nor shorted but behaves outside its expected range, for example current that does not track the command. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: MIL on
Inconsistent shift quality on the affected rods

P27C7.d: P27C7 points to a control circuit of solenoid P that is too low, effectively a short to ground on the switched side. GM's 23OBDG07 Corvette dual-clutch table checks synchronizer actuation valve 3 with its low-side switch on and expects the sense resistor voltage to be pulled down only so far; a reading under about 1.7 V (±0.5 V) for 150 ms is reported by the driver chip as a ground short, Type A, provided the engine
s: MIL on
Unwanted application of rods 3/4, gears blocked
Limp mode
c: Control wire shorted to ground against the case
Moisture or oil bridging pins in the connector
Solenoid winding shorted to its housing

P27C8.d: P27C8 signals too high a level in the control circuit of solenoid P. GM's Corvette DCT tables 23OBDG07 and 24OBDG07 store it for synchronizer actuation valve 3 in three situations, all Type A.
s: MIL on, possibly at the start after a previous drive
Gears of rods 3/4 unavailable
Limp mode
c: Control line shorted to battery voltage
Control line shorted to a neighbouring solenoid output
Solenoid P coil with too low resistance (shorted turns)

P27C9.d: Solenoid R is the fourth synchronizer pressure valve on the dual-clutch units that use it, and P27C9 says it failed to move anything. GM's 2023 and 2024 Corvette tables (23OBDG07/24OBDG07) call it shift solenoid 4; it acts on the same two rods as valve 3 but drives them back from B towards A.
s: MIL on with transmission message
Gear stays engaged or cannot be selected
Reduced gear range
c: Spool of solenoid R stuck closed
Supply passage or screen to valve R clogged by debris
Leaking actuator seal on the B-to-A side of rods 3/4

P27CA.d: P27CA is the stuck-on fault of solenoid R, GM's shift solenoid 4 on the Corvette dual-clutch transmission. The detection in 23OBDG07 mirrors that of valve 3 because both valves share rods 3 and 4, only with opposite pushing direction: a selector change followed by an uncommanded jump of one rod of at least 1 mm inside 200 ms plus a 0.125 mm relaxation of its partner points to valve 4 holding pressure.
s: MIL on
Grinding or clunk when changing gears
Gears locked out by the controller
c: Spool of solenoid R jammed open
Debris lodged in valve R preventing venting
Internal wear of solenoid R armature or seat

P27CB.d: An electrical fault of unspecified kind on solenoid R is what P27CB stands for. There is no public manufacturer description of this exact code.
s: MIL on
Gear selection limited
Emergency mode possible
c: Solenoid R winding resistance out of specification
Poor pin fit in the gearbox connector

P27CC.d: With P27CC the transmission controller has seen solenoid R lose its circuit or its effect for short moments only. A public, code-specific manufacturer description does not exist.
s: Intermittent MIL
Sporadic rough or delayed shift
c: Transmission fluid wicking into the connector

P27CD.d: P27CD is set when the control circuit of solenoid R appears open, so the module cannot energize the valve. On GM's Corvette with dual-clutch transmission (23OBDG07, again in 24OBDG07) the part is synchronizer actuation valve 4.
s: MIL on
Shifts on rods 3 and 4 in B-to-A direction not possible
Limp mode
c: Terminal pushed out of the connector housing

P27CE.d: P27CE would be stored if the control circuit of solenoid R stayed electrically connected yet produced values that make no sense to the controller. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: MIL on
Shift feel varies on rods 3 and 4
c: Rising contact resistance in the circuit
Solenoid R with partly shorted turns

P27CF.d: P27CF tells that the control line of solenoid R is held low, as if shorted to ground. On the Corvette dual-clutch transmission GM (23OBDG07, still present in 24OBDG07) monitors synchronizer actuation valve 4 while energized; the driver chip compares the sense pin with a threshold of roughly 1.7 V and, after 150 ms below it, reports a ground fault rated Type A.
s: MIL on
Unwanted rod movement, gears locked out
Limp mode
c: Chafed insulation grounding the control line
Harness crushed at a clip or bracket
Solenoid R coil shorted to its housing

P27D0.d: P27D0 is the high-side counterpart of P27CF for solenoid R: the control line reads too high, most often because it touches battery voltage or another output. GM applies the same driver diagnostics to synchronizer actuation valve 4 of the Corvette dual-clutch box as to the other valves (23OBDG07, 24OBDG07): a sense voltage stuck above 0.7-1.1 V while switched on, a large gap between target and estimated current, or a
s: MIL on, sometimes only after restart
Gears on rods 3/4 not available
Limp mode
c: Cross-short to a neighbouring solenoid line
Solenoid R coil resistance too low

P27D1.d: P27D1 flags pressure control solenoid S as unable to produce force. Only GM documents it publicly: in the Corvette dual-clutch tables 23OBDG07 and 24OBDG07 it is shift solenoid 5, the only one of these valves serving a single rod, rod 5, which it moves in both directions depending on the selector position.
s: MIL on
Gears on rod 5 unavailable
Gearbox in substitute mode
c: Spool of solenoid S sticking closed
Leak at the rod 5 actuator piston

P27D2.d: With P27D2 the TCM concludes that solenoid S applies pressure that was never requested. GM is the only maker publishing it, for shift solenoid 5 of the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox (23OBDG07, carried over to 24OBDG07).
s: MIL on
Harsh engagement or clunk
Gears on rod 5 blocked, fallback mode
c: Spool of solenoid S jammed open
Particles keeping valve S from venting
Worn armature or seat in solenoid S

P27D3.d: P27D3 reports an electrical problem with pressure control solenoid S without saying which kind. No manufacturer publishes this code.
s: MIL on
Gears on rod 5 unavailable
Limp mode possible
c: Solenoid S coil open or shorted
Corroded or loose connector at the transmission
Damaged wiring between TCM and solenoid S

P27D4.d: P27D4 means the controller noticed solenoid S dropping out now and then, electrically or in its effect, without the fault staying present. No manufacturer publishes this code.
s: MIL comes and goes
Rod 5 gears occasionally refused
c: Gearbox connector seal leaking, terminals corroding
Harness conductor breaking under engine movement
Solenoid S winding dropping out when hot

P27D5.d: P27D5 stands for an interrupted control circuit of solenoid S. GM uses it for synchronizer actuation valve 5 in the Corvette DCT, documented in 23OBDG07 and again in 24OBDG07.
s: MIL on
Gears on rod 5 missing
Emergency program
c: Terminal pushed back in the gearbox connector
Broken control wire between TCM and valve

P27D6.d: P27D6 would indicate that the circuit of solenoid S is still closed but its electrical behaviour does not fit what the module commands. There is no public manufacturer description.
s: MIL on
Uneven shifts into rod 5 gears
c: Added resistance at a crimp or pin
Solenoid S coil resistance out of specification

P27D7.d: P27D7 reports the control line of solenoid S stuck at too low a level, typically a short to ground. GM applies it to synchronizer actuation valve 5 on the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox (23OBDG07, carried into 24OBDG07): with the output switched on, the sense pin should be pulled down only partly; if it drops below roughly 1.7 V and stays there 150 ms, the driver chip flags a ground short and the TCM stores a Type A fa
s: MIL on
Unintended rod 5 movement, gears locked
Limp mode
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Solenoid S coil shorted to its housing
Faulty low-side driver in the TCM

P27D8.d: P27D8 says the control line of solenoid S sits too high. GM bundles three checks for valve 5 of the Corvette dual-clutch box under it (23OBDG07, 24OBDG07), all Type A.
s: MIL on, possibly only after the next start
Rod 5 gears out of reach
Limp mode
c: Control wire touching a supply line
Short to the wire of another valve output
Solenoid S coil with shorted turns

P27D9.d: P27D9 is logged when solenoid T fails to build the pressure it is asked for. Ford's 2024 OBD overview for the TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox assigns it to the selector pilot valve (SELPV) when that valve stays hydraulically off.
s: MIL on
Several gears unavailable
Gearbox in fallback mode
c: Selector valve spool binding in its bore

P27DA.d: P27DA marks solenoid T as delivering pressure while it should be vented. Ford lists it in the 2024 overview for the TR9070 for a selector pilot valve whose hydraulic output stays on; neighbouring entries P178C and P178A cover the selector valve and the complete selector mechanism stuck on.
s: MIL on
Gears locked out, wrong gear engagement possible
Fallback mode
c: Selector pilot valve held open by dirt
Worn seat or armature in solenoid T
Abrasion particles from clutch or synchronizer wear

P27DB.d: P27DB is a catch-all for electrical trouble on solenoid T that does not name the kind of fault. No manufacturer publishes it.
s: MIL on
Restricted gear choice
Limp mode possible
c: Solenoid T coil open or shorted
Corrosion or poor fit at the gearbox connector
Defective TCM output for solenoid T

P27DC.d: With P27DC the module reports that solenoid T misbehaved only briefly before working again. No maker has published a description of this code.
s: MIL lights up from time to time
Occasional failed or late gear selection
c: Loose pin in the gearbox connector
Particles briefly holding the valve spool

P27DD.d: P27DD tells that the control circuit of solenoid T is open, so no current reaches the coil. Ford's 2024 OBD overview gives this code to open load on the selector pilot valve of the TR9070 dual-clutch transmission; the document lists the fault type only, without limits.
s: MIL on
Only some gears selectable
Fallback mode

P27DE.d: P27DE would be set if the circuit of solenoid T is intact but delivers readings the controller considers implausible. No manufacturer documents the code.
s: MIL on
Hesitant or inconsistent gear selection
c: Rising contact resistance at a terminal
Solenoid T resistance drifted from nominal
TCM output no longer regulating current

P27DF.d: P27DF points to a control line of solenoid T pulled too low. In Ford's 2024 OBD summary it is the shorted-switch fault of the selector pilot valve on the TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox, meaning the switched side of the coil is tied to ground and the valve can be powered permanently.
s: MIL on
Gears fenced off, shifts limited to some gears
Limp mode
c: Damaged insulation letting the wire touch ground
Solenoid T coil shorted to ground

P27E0.d: P27E0 reports a control line of solenoid T sitting too high. Ford's 2024 overview of the TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox uses it for a shorted load on the selector pilot valve, a coil or line bypassed to battery so the driver cannot pull current through the winding.
s: MIL on
Gears of one rod group lost
Fallback mode
c: Control wire shorted to a supply feed
Cross-short to an adjacent valve line

P27E1.d: P27E1 is a hydraulic verdict, not a wiring one: electric auxiliary pump A was running on command, yet the pressure it built stayed below what the module expected. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: Stop-start function disabled
Jerky or delayed engagement when the engine restarts after a stop
MIL or transmission warning lit
c: Worn pump gears or internal leakage inside pump A
Low or aerated transmission fluid, pump draws air
Intake screen of the pump partly blocked by debris
Check valve in the pump circuit not sealing

P27E2.d: P27E2 flags that the second electric pump, B, delivered too little pressure although it was driven. Nobody publishes this code openly.
s: Stop-start no longer stops the engine
Reduced clutch cooling, power limited when hot
Warning light on
c: Pump B worn, motor running but delivering too little
Leaking O-ring or pressure line between pump B and the gearbox
Fluid level too low for pump B to prime
Weak battery or poor ground slowing the pump motor

P27E3.d: The control valve named here decides where the oil from the electric auxiliary pump goes. Volkswagen's training book for the 0GC seven-speed DSG shows such a layout: pressure regulator N218 shifts a spring-loaded changeover piston that sends the flow of pump V475 either to the mechatronic unit or to clutch cooling.
s: Stop-start unavailable
Warning light with stored open-circuit fault
c: Broken conductor in the valve control line
Pin backed out or corroded at the gearbox connector

P27E4.d: P27E4 is the plausibility check for the auxiliary pump control valve: the circuit is intact, but its current or its hydraulic effect does not match the command. No manufacturer lists the code publicly, so the logic can only be inferred.
s: Stop-start works only sometimes
Harsh engagement after an auto-start
Warning light on
c: Valve or changeover piston sticking from contaminated fluid
Contact resistance at the connector distorting the current

P27E5.d: P27E5 sets when the voltage on the auxiliary pump control valve line is pulled toward ground, typically by chafed insulation touching the case or by a coil shorted internally. No manufacturer documents the code openly.
s: Stop-start switched off
MIL lit
c: Control line chafed through and touching ground
Fluid or water in the connector bridging to ground

P27E6.d: P27E6 means the control valve circuit of the auxiliary pump reads higher than allowed, as if the line were tied to battery voltage. A wire rubbing against a live conductor in the same harness, or a driver stage that no longer switches off, are the classic triggers.
s: Stop-start inoperative
Warning light on, possibly further pump codes
c: Control line shorted to a supply wire in the harness
Output stage in the control module stuck on
Corrosion bridging adjacent pins in the connector

P27E7.d: 'Transmission Range Control' belongs to shift-by-wire, where the selected range travels as an electrical signal instead of a cable. Only channel A is documented in public: Mitsubishi's 2022 manual sets P07E8 when one of eight electric shift sensors in the selector rises above 4.5 V for 2.4 s with the ignition on, and names no fail-safe reaction.
s: Warning about the shift system in the cluster
Some ranges not accepted from the selector
c: Loose or corroded connector at the electric selector
Broken wire between selector and control module
Sensor inside the selector assembly failed open

P27E8.d: P27E8 is the plausibility test for range control circuit B: the signal is neither open nor shorted, yet its value makes no sense, for example a level stuck between the valid on and off windows. The title reads Circuit Performance, without Range.
s: Intermittent shift system warning
Displayed range occasionally flickers or lags
c: Contact resistance at selector terminals shifting the voltage
Spilled drink or moisture inside the selector
Position sensor in the selector degrading

P27E9.d: P27E9 reports that a line of range control circuit B sits too close to zero volts, pointing to a grounded line or a sensor that pulls its output down. It is not described publicly by any manufacturer.
s: Shift system warning on the display
Usually no change in how the car drives
c: Harness pinched under the center console, shorted to ground
Sensor supply interrupted, output drops to zero

P27EA.d: With P27EA, a signal of range control circuit B reads near the supply voltage, which usually means a short to a power wire or a broken ground return that lets the line float high. No manufacturer documents the B code openly.
s: Shift system message in the cluster
Car usually still drives normally
c: Signal line shorted to a supply wire
Sensor ground open, signal floats high

P27EB.d: GM uses this code on automatics with internal electronic range selection (ETRS), where hydraulic mode valves within the valve body set park, reverse, neutral and drive. Mode valve A carries a Hall position sensor.
s: MIL on after the first trip
Range selection restricted or delayed
c: Signal wire of the mode valve A sensor broken or loose
Hall sensor on mode valve A failing
Damaged internal transmission harness or pass-through connector

P27EC.d: P27EC is GM's movement check for mode valve A of its internal range selection: after the TCM commands park, drive or reverse, the position sensor must report the new state within a set delay; the logic also watches line pressure and clutch slip. Both the 2018 nine-speed and 2020 ten-speed tables rate it Type A.
s: Delayed or refused shift into park, drive or reverse
MIL on, stop-start may be disabled
Transmission in reduced operating mode
c: Mode valve A sticking inside the control valve body
No hydraulic pressure from a failed auxiliary pump during auto stop
Mode valve A position sensor reading wrong

P27ED.d: P27ED tells that the Hall sensor on mode valve A of GM's internal range selection delivers almost no voltage. In both the 2018 9-speed and the 2020 10-speed RWD tables the limit is a raw value under 0.414 V for 0.100 s within 0.163 s, with at least 9 V on the battery; GM itself blames a grounded or interrupted line.
s: MIL lit immediately
Shifts out of park slow or blocked
c: Sensor signal shorted to ground in the internal harness
Hall sensor on mode valve A failed

P27EE.d: The opposite of P27ED: the position sensor of mode valve A reads higher than any valid state. GM's TCM tables for the T87A nine-speed of 2018 and the rear-drive ten-speed of 2020 set P27EE when the raw signal exceeds 2.538 V for 0.100 s inside a 0.163 s sample, describing it as a short to voltage on the sensor circuit; the MIL comes on at once (Type A).
s: MIL on from the first trip
Range changes restricted, possible reduced mode
c: Sensor signal shorted to a voltage source
Sensor ground open, signal drifts high

P27EF.d: P27EF concerns the second mode valve, B, of GM's internal electronic range selection. Its Hall sensor is expected to sit clearly high or clearly low; GM's 2018 9-speed and 2020 10-speed RWD tables treat a raw value between 1.263 and 1.504 V, held for 0.100 s of a 0.163 s sample, as an illegal level.
s: Transmission warning, neutral or drive engagement may be restricted
Fault stored in the TCM
c: Mode valve B sensor signal line interrupted
Hall sensor on mode valve B no longer switching cleanly
Fluid or corrosion at the transmission pass-through connector

P27F0.d: P27F0 checks whether mode valve B really moves. In GM's 2020 table for the T87A 10-speed RWD transmission, the TCM expects the valve B sensor to follow commands to park, reverse, neutral high or low, neutral shift and drive within a delay; if the final state is not reached under adequate line pressure, the Type A code sets.
s: Delay or refusal when selecting neutral, drive or reverse
MIL on, transmission may enter a protective mode
c: Mode valve B sticking in the valve body
Insufficient line pressure to move the valve
Position sensor B reporting late or wrong state

P27F1.d: P27F1 reports a valve B position signal that has collapsed toward ground in GM's internal range selection. GM describes the trigger as a ground short or open circuit on the mode valve B sensor line and uses the same 0.414 V limit, 0.100 s debounce and 9 V minimum supply as on valve A; both table editions, 2018 and 2020, rate it Type A, MIL on the first trip.
s: MIL comes on on the first trip
Neutral or drive engagement slow or blocked
c: Valve B sensor line shorted to ground
Sensor supply missing at the internal connector
Hall sensor on mode valve B failed

P27F2.d: With P27F2 the TCM sees the valve B position sensor above its valid range, which GM interprets as a short to voltage on that circuit. The threshold is 2.538 V, which must persist 0.100 s in a 0.163 s sampling period; GM applies it to internal range selection in the 2018 T87A nine-speed and the 2020 rear-drive ten-speed.
s: Warning light and stored transmission fault
Neutral or drive selection restricted
c: Valve B sensor line shorted to a voltage source

P27F3.d: P27F3 reports that the second clutch of a gearbox, usually the clutch on the even-gear side of a dual-clutch unit, has exceeded its permitted temperature, either measured or calculated from slip and load. Stellantis is the one maker with a public, code-exact document: bulletin 21-040-26 (May 2026) lists P27F3-00 as clutch 2 overtemperature on European 2022-2025 Jeep Renegade and Compass with the 1.5 L mild hybrid and
s: Malfunction indicator and transmission warning lamp on
Even gears or reverse temporarily unavailable
Judder or burning smell when pulling away
c: Pump in the electric clutch actuator blocked by particles
Long slipping phases from creeping, towing or hill starts
Worn clutch 2 that needs more slip to transmit torque
Insufficient clutch cooling or low or aged fluid

P27F4.d: P27F4 concerns the mechanical result of the shift lock, not its wiring: actuator A was commanded but stays in its active state or does not reach the requested position. Whether active means locked or released depends on the design.
s: Selector cannot be moved out of Park despite pressing the brake
Shift system warning or wrench lamp in the cluster
Clicking from the shifter with no release
c: Lock pin or actuator binding in the shifter mechanism
Faulty gear shift module or its software
Implausible brake pedal signal keeping the lock commanded

P27F5.d: With P27F5 the control unit concludes that shift lock actuator A remains in its passive state although it was told to act. Depending on the design, that can leave the lever free to leave Park without the brake, which defeats the brake interlock, or permanently blocked.
s: Selector leaves Park without the brake pedal being pressed
Lever stays blocked in Park or Neutral
Shift system warning message
c: Loose or badly crimped terminal at the lock solenoid
Weak solenoid coil that no longer moves the lock pin
Broken return spring or worn lock pin
Shifter module software misjudging the actuator position
